Qwen3.5-397B-A17B        *sglang-model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b*

  Note: ~

  This page focuses on optimal configuration and benchmark results for
  Qwen3.5-397B-A17B on the Ascend NPU. For environment setup, model weight
  download, feature configuration, and deployment instructions, etc., see
  the |sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-qwen3_5_397b|.

  On the A3 Series, each card has 2 dies, so `--tp-size` is twice the card
  count; see |ascend-npus-reference-glossary-hardware| for details.

          *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b-optimal-configuration*
OPTIMAL CONFIGURATION

*model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b-qwen3-5-397b-a17b-w4a8-8p-in128k-out1k-20ms*
Qwen3.5-397B-A17B W4A8 8P IN128K OUT1K 20ms

Model: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B

Hardware: A3 Series Products

Cards: 8

Deploy Mode: PD Mixed

Quantization: W4A8 INT8

Dataset: 128k+1k

TPOT: 20ms

               *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b-model-deployment*
Model Deployment

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    # ============================================================

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights
    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy
    unset HTTPS_PROXY
    unset HTTP_PROXY
    unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING

    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=4096
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=32
    export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
    export GDN_ATTN_BACKEND_TRITON=1
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=0
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=128
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
    export SGLANG_ZBAL_BOOTSTRAP_URL=tcp://127.0.0.1:24669
    export SGLANG_ZBAL_LOCAL_MEM_SIZE=60672
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export ZBAL_ENABLE_GRAPH=1
    export ZBAL_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=use_vmm_for_static_memory:True

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --tp-size 16 \
        --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
        --max-prefill-tokens 131072 \
        --prefill-max-requests 1 \
        --disable-radix-cache \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --max-running-requests 16 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.6 \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 2 3 4 5 6 8 10 12 14 16 \
        --quantization modelslim \
        --enable-multimodal \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
        --deepep-mode auto \
        --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn \
        --dtype bfloat16 \
        --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
        --speculative-num-steps 3 \
        --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
        --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
        --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
        --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
<

Benchmark             *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b-benchmark*

We tested it based on the `RANDOM` dataset.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --dataset-name random \
        --backend sglang \
        --host 127.0.0.1 \
        --port 6688 \
        --warmup-requests 2 \
        --max-concurrency 3 \
        --num-prompts 3 \
        --random-input-len 131072 \
        --random-output-len 1024 \
        --random-range-ratio 1 \
        --seed 1 \
        --request-rate inf

Benchmark           *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b-benchmark-3*

We tested it based on the `generated-shared-prefix` dataset with 90% cache
hit (`repeat_rate = 0.9`): `--gsp-system-prompt-len 117965` =
`round(131072 * 0.9)` is the shared prefix portion.
`--gsp-question-len 13107` = `round(131072 * (1 - 0.9))` is the unique
per-request suffix. `--gsp-num-groups 1` keeps all requests in one prefix
group for maximum cache reuse.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
        --backend sglang \
        --host 127.0.0.1 \
        --port 6688 \
        --gsp-num-groups 1 \
        --gsp-prompts-per-group 40 \
        --gsp-system-prompt-len 117965 \
        --gsp-question-len 13107 \
        --gsp-output-len 1024 \
        --max-concurrency 40 \
        --num-prompts 40 \
        --request-rate inf
<

Benchmark          *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_5_397b-benchmark-10*

We tested it based on the `generated-shared-prefix` dataset with 90% cache
hit (`repeat_rate = 0.9`): `--gsp-system-prompt-len 58982` =
`round(65536 * 0.9)` is the shared prefix portion. `--gsp-question-len 6554`
= `round(65536 * (1 - 0.9))` is the unique per-request suffix.
`--gsp-num-groups 1` keeps all requests in one prefix group for maximum
cache reuse.

[Command]Command

>sh
    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
        --backend sglang \
        --host 127.0.0.1 \
        --port 6688 \
        --gsp-num-groups 1 \
        --gsp-prompts-per-group 96 \
        --gsp-system-prompt-len 58982 \
        --gsp-question-len 6554 \
        --gsp-output-len 1024 \
        --max-concurrency 96 \
        --num-prompts 96 \
        --request-rate inf

Benchmark            *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_6_27b-benchmark-3*

We tested it based on the `generated-shared-prefix` dataset with 90% cache
hit (`repeat_rate = 0.9`): `--gsp-system-prompt-len 57600` =
`round(64000 * 0.9)` is the shared prefix portion. `--gsp-question-len 6400`
= `round(64000 * (1 - 0.9))` is the unique per-request suffix.
`--gsp-num-groups 1` keeps all requests in one prefix group for maximum
cache reuse.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
        --backend sglang \
        --host 127.0.0.1 \
        --port 6688 \
        --gsp-num-groups 1 \
        --gsp-prompts-per-group 20 \
        --gsp-system-prompt-len 57600 \
        --gsp-question-len 6400 \
        --gsp-output-len 1000 \
        --max-concurrency 20 \
        --num-prompts 20 \
        --request-rate inf
<

            *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_6_35b_a3b-model-deployment*
Model Deployment

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    # ============================================================

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights
    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy
    unset HTTPS_PROXY
    unset HTTP_PROXY
    unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING

    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
    export SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \
        --tp-size 2 \
        --nnodes 1 \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
        --max-prefill-tokens 9999999 \
        --max-total-tokens 365000 \
        --prefill-max-requests 30 \
        --disable-radix-cache \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --max-running-requests 120 \
        --max-mamba-cache-size 120 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 4 16 32 48 64 110 165 \
        --enable-multimodal \
        --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn \
        --dtype bfloat16 \
        --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
        --speculative-num-steps 3 \
        --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
        --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
        --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder

Benchmark        *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_6_35b_a3b-benchmark-4*

We tested it based on the `generated-shared-prefix` dataset with 90% cache
hit (`repeat_rate = 0.9`): `--gsp-system-prompt-len 115200` =
`round(128000 * 0.9)` is the shared prefix portion.
`--gsp-question-len 12800` = `round(128000 * (1 - 0.9))` is the unique
per-request suffix. `--gsp-num-groups 1` keeps all requests in one prefix
group for maximum cache reuse.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
        --backend sglang \
        --host 127.0.0.1 \
        --port 6688 \
        --gsp-num-groups 1 \
        --gsp-prompts-per-group 412 \
        --gsp-system-prompt-len 115200 \
        --gsp-question-len 12800 \
        --gsp-output-len 1000 \
        --max-concurrency 103 \
        --num-prompts 412 \
        --request-rate inf

Benchmark        *model-deployment-best-practices-qwen3_6_35b_a3b-benchmark-8*

We tested it based on the `generated-shared-prefix` dataset with 90% cache
hit (`repeat_rate = 0.9`): `--gsp-system-prompt-len 58982` =
`round(65536 * 0.9)` is the shared prefix portion. `--gsp-question-len 6554`
= `round(65536 * (1 - 0.9))` is the unique per-request suffix.
`--gsp-num-groups 1` keeps all requests in one prefix group for maximum
cache reuse.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
        --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix \
        --backend sglang \
        --host 127.0.0.1 \
        --port 6688 \
        --gsp-num-groups 1 \
        --gsp-prompts-per-group 40 \
        --gsp-system-prompt-len 58982 \
        --gsp-question-len 6554 \
        --gsp-output-len 1024 \
        --max-concurrency 40 \
        --num-prompts 40 \
        --request-rate inf

    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    #   DRAFT_MODEL_PATH: path to the draft model weights directory
    #   HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for HCCL
    #   GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for Gloo
    # ============================================================

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights
    DRAFT_MODEL_PATH=/path/to/draft-model-weights

    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy

    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --enable-prefill-delayer \

[Command]Command

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    #   DRAFT_MODEL_PATH: path to the draft model weights directory
    #   HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for HCCL
    #   GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for Gloo
    # ============================================================

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights
    DRAFT_MODEL_PATH=/path/to/draft-model-weights

    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy
    unset HTTPS_PROXY
    unset HTTP_PROXY
    unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING

    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
    export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2000
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=2048
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=10
    export FORCE_DRAFT_MODEL_NON_QUANT=1
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=400
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0
    export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=0
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
    export SGLANG_WARMUP_TIMEOUT=3600
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=1
    export ZBCCL_BOOTSTRAP_URL=tcp://127.0.0.1:24669
    export ZBCCL_ENABLE_GRAPH=1
    export ZBCCL_LOCAL_MEM_SIZE=60416
    export ZBCCL_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=use_vmm_for_static_memory:True

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --quantization modelslim \
        --page-size 128 \
        --tp-size 2 \
        --watchdog-timeout 9000 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
        --disable-radix-cache \
        --max-prefill-tokens 28672 \
        --context-length 26384 \
        --max-total-tokens 122304 \
        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
        --speculative-num-steps 3 \
        --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
        --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
        --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
        --max-running-requests 2 \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 2 \
        --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
        --speculative-draft-model-path $DRAFT_MODEL_PATH \
        --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
        --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
DeepSeek-R1                    *sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1*

INTRODUCTION             *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-introduction*

DeepSeek-R1 is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model developed by
DeepSeek, featuring 671B total parameters with 37B active parameters. It
employs Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE architecture, with
built-in multi-token prediction (MTP) for speculative decoding. The model
excels at reasoning, math, and code tasks through reinforcement
learning-based training.

This document demonstrates the deployment of DeepSeek-R1 on Ascend NPUs
using SGLang, including single-node PD mixed mode, multi-node PD
disaggregation mode, feature configuration, and performance optimization.

The commands in this document use the daily build image
`quay.io/ascend/sglang:main-cann9.1.0-a3`.

SUPPORTED FEATURES *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-supported-features*

Feature               Example usage
--------------------  --------------------------------------------------------
Tensor Parallelism    --tp-size 16
Data Parallelism      --dp-size 16
Expert Parallelism    --ep-size 16 \--moe-a2a-backend deepep \--deepep-mode
                      auto
PD Disaggregation     --disaggregation-mode prefill
                      \--disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend
Quantization          --quantization modelslim
NPU Graph             enabled by default; disable with
                      --disable-decode-cuda-graph
                      --disable-prefill-cuda-graph;control range via
                      --cuda-graph-bs-decode or --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode;
                      e.g., --cuda-graph-bs-decode 4 8 20 21 22
Speculative Decoding  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \--speculative-num-steps 2
                      \--speculative-eagle-topk 1
                      \--speculative-num-draft-tokens 3
Overlap Schedule      export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
DP LM Head            --enable-dp-lm-head
MLAPO                 export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MLAPO=1
Multistream MoE       export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1
NZ Weight Format      export SGLANG_USE_FIA_NZ=1

  Note: ~

  The values in the Example usage column are for illustration only. Adjust
  them according to your hardware, deployment mode, and workload. For
  parameter details, see
  |ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning-parameter-reference|; for
  recommended configurations for each deployment scenario, see
  |model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-best-practices|.

For feature compatibility and conflict information between features, see
|ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning-feature-compatibility|.

PREREQUISITES           *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-prerequisites*

Environment               *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-environment*

Before following this tutorial, complete the environment setup in the
documents below:

- |sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-quick_start| --- the fastest way to
  get started. It walks you through launching the official container image,
  starting the SGLang server, and sending a test request. Recommended if you
  are new to SGLang on Ascend.
- |sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-installation| --- the full
  installation guide. It covers the component version mapping (CANN,
  TorchNPU, Triton, kernels, etc.), building from source or from a
  Dockerfile, and recommended system settings (CPU power scheme, NUMA,
  swap). Use it when you need to install or customize the environment
  instead of using the official image.

Model weights           *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-model-weights*

Before downloading model weights, check the model size to reserve enough
disk space. For multi-node deployment, download the weights to a shared
directory accessible to all nodes.

- DeepSeek-R1-0528-W4A8
  https://modelers.cn/models/Modelers_Park/DeepSeek-R1-0528-w4a8 (Quantized
  version, 376GB)
- DeepSeek-R1-0528-W8A8
  https://modelers.cn/models/Modelers_Park/DeepSeek-R1-0528-w8a8 (Quantized
  version, 647GB)

  Info: ~

  The W4A8 variant (376GB) can be deployed on 8 × 64GB of device memory
  (`--tp-size 8`), which corresponds to 8 dies on an A3 Series node (4
  cards).

  The W8A8 variant (647GB) can be deployed on 16 × 64GB of device memory
  (`--tp-size 16`), which corresponds to one full A3 Series node (8 cards,
  16 dies).

This is the minimum recommended configuration. For optimized configurations,
see |model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-best-practices|, which may
require additional cards or nodes.

For the hardware specifications (memory per die and dies per card), see
|ascend-npus-reference-glossary-hardware|.

  Warning: ~

    default name.

            *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-online-service-deployment*
ONLINE SERVICE DEPLOYMENT

        *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-single-node-online-deployment*
Single-node online deployment

Single-node deployment completes both prefill and decode within the same
node (PD mixed mode), suitable for scenarios with limited hardware
resources. This scenario is already covered in the best practice. For the
complete, optimized deployment commands and benchmark data, see
|model-deployment-best-practices-deepseek_r1-single-node-pd-mixed|.

*model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-multi-node-pd-disaggregation-deployment*
Multi-node PD disaggregation deployment

PD disaggregation splits the prefill and decode stages onto separate nodes,
reducing interference and improving throughput for high-concurrency
scenarios. This scenario is already covered in the best practice. For the
complete, optimized deployment commands and benchmark data, see
|model-deployment-best-practices-deepseek_r1-pd-disaggregation|.

              *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_r1-functional-verification*
FUNCTIONAL VERIFICATION

After the service is started, you can invoke the model by sending a prompt:

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   HOST: the server host address (e.g., localhost)
    #   PORT: the server port number (e.g., 6689)
    # ============================================================

    curl http://${HOST}:${PORT}/generate \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{
            "text": "What is the capital of France?",
            "sampling_params": {
                "max_new_tokens": 64,
                "temperature": 0
            }
        }'
<
Expected result: an HTTP 200 response with the generated text containing
“Paris”.

Once the server prints `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` in the
logs, it is ready to accept requests. For more testing examples (Health
Check, Generate, Chat Completions, and port usage guidance), see
|ascend-npus-getting-started-installation-testing-the-service|.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
DeepSeek-V3.2                *sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v3_2*

INTRODUCTION           *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v3_2-introduction*

DeepSeek-V3.2 is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model developed
by DeepSeek, featuring 685B total parameters with 37B active parameters. It
employs Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and DeepSeekMoE architecture, with
built-in multi-token prediction (MTP) for speculative decoding.
DeepSeek-V3.2 introduces the DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) mechanism, a
fine-grained sparse attention mechanism powered by a lightning indexer,
enabling significant efficiency improvements in long-context scenarios.

This document demonstrates the deployment of DeepSeek-V3.2 on Ascend NPUs
using SGLang, including multi-node PD disaggregation mode, feature
configuration, and performance optimization.

The commands in this document use the daily build image
`quay.io/ascend/sglang:main-cann9.1.0-a3`.

            *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v3_2-functional-verification*
FUNCTIONAL VERIFICATION

After the service is started, you can invoke the model by sending a prompt:

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   HOST: the server host address (e.g., localhost)
    #   PORT: the server port number (e.g., 6689)
    # ============================================================

    curl http://${HOST}:${PORT}/generate \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{
            "text": "What is the capital of France?",
            "sampling_params": {
                "max_new_tokens": 64,
                "temperature": 0
            }
        }'
<
Expected result: an HTTP 200 response with the generated text containing
“Paris”.

Once the server prints `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` in the
logs, it is ready to accept requests. For more testing examples (Health
Check, Generate, Chat Completions, and port usage guidance), see
|ascend-npus-getting-started-installation-testing-the-service|.

DeepSeek-V4-Flash        *sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash*

INTRODUCTION       *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-introduction*

DeepSeek-V4-Flash is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model
developed by DeepSeek, featuring 284B total parameters with 13B active
parameters. It employs hybrid sparse attention (CSA + HCA) and DeepSeekMoE
architecture with a bundled multi-token prediction (MTP) draft head for
speculative decoding, supporting a 1M-token context length.

This document demonstrates the deployment of DeepSeek-V4-Flash on Ascend
NPUs using SGLang, covering both the A3 Series and the 950PR/DT Series (SoC
name A5), including single-node PD mixed deployment, multi-node PD
disaggregation mode, feature configuration, and performance optimization.

This document is validated and written based on SGLang v0.5.16. The current
model (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) is fully supported in this version. To use the
latest features (e.g., PD disaggregation, speculative decoding), it is
recommended to use v0.5.16 or a later version.

             *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-supported-features*
SUPPORTED FEATURES

Feature               Example usage
--------------------  --------------------------------------------------------
Attention Backend     --attention-backend dsv4
Tensor Parallelism    --tp-size 16
Data Parallelism      --dp-size 16
Expert Parallelism    --ep-size 16 \--moe-a2a-backend deepep \--deepep-mode
                      auto
PD Disaggregation     --disaggregation-mode prefill
                      \--disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend
Quantization          --quantization modelslim
NPU Graph             enabled by default; disable with
                      --disable-decode-cuda-graph
                      --disable-prefill-cuda-graph;control range via
                      --cuda-graph-bs-decode or --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode;
                      e.g., --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 24 36 40 48 56
Speculative Decoding  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \--speculative-num-steps 2
                      \--speculative-eagle-topk 1
                      \--speculative-num-draft-tokens 3
Overlap Schedule      export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
DP LM Head            --enable-dp-lm-head
DP Attention          --attn-dp-size 16

  Note: ~

  The values in the Example usage column are for illustration only. Adjust
  them according to your hardware, deployment mode, and workload. For
  parameter details, see

  |model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-best-practices|.

For feature compatibility and conflict information between features, see

ONLINE SERVICE DEPLOYMENT

*model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-single-node-pd-mixed-deployment*
Single-node PD mixed deployment

Single-node deployment completes both prefill and decode within the same
node (PD mixed mode), suitable for scenarios with limited hardware
resources. Select the script for your platform and run it inside the
container.

A3 Series           *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-a3-series-2*

DeepSeek-V4-Flash can be launched with half of an A3 Series node (4 cards, 8
dies). The configuration below was validated with `--tp-size 8`.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variable:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    # ============================================================

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights

    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/opp/vendors/customize/bin/set_env.bash
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/opp/vendors/custom_transformer/bin/set_env.bash

    export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
    export FORCE_DRAFT_MODEL_NON_QUANT=1
    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=8
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    export INF_NAN_MODE_FORCE_DISABLE=1
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=False
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=0
    export SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO=torch
    export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=0
    export SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_WQA_WKV=0
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_HASH_TOPK=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_OVERLAP_STORE_CACHE=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=False
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
    export SGLANG_ZBAL_BOOTSTRAP_URL="tcp://127.0.0.1:14699"
    export SGLANG_ZBAL_LOCAL_MEM_SIZE=62084
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export ZBAL_ENABLE_GRAPH=1
    export ZBAL_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=use_vmm_for_static_memory:True

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
        --page-size 128 \
        --tp-size 8 \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --device npu \
        --attention-backend dsv4 \
        --watchdog-timeout 9000 \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
        --prefill-max-requests 160 \
        --max-prefill-tokens 80000 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 131072 \
        --max-running-requests 160 \
        --attn-dp-size 8 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --quantization modelslim --enable-dp-lm-head \
        --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
<

            *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-950pr%2Fdt-series-2*
950PR/DT Series

The 950PR/DT Series (SoC name A5) exposes one device per card, and
DeepSeek-V4-Flash can be launched with half of a node (4 cards). Use the
native `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` checkpoint. The configuration below was
validated with `--tp-size 4` and DSPARK speculative decoding.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variable:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    # ============================================================

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights

    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/opp/vendors/customize/bin/set_env.bash
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/opp/vendors/custom_transformer/bin/set_env.bash

    export ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH=/usr/local/Ascend/extra-ops/vendors/custom_transformer/:$ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH
    export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1600
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_COMBINE_ENABLE_LONG_SEQ=1
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=2048
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=16
    export FORCE_DRAFT_MODEL_NON_QUANT=1
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/Ascend/extra-ops/vendors/custom_transformer/op_api/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=160
    export SGLANG_DSPARK_A5_EXTRA_OPS_SO=/usr/local/Ascend/extra-ops/vllm_ascend_C.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so
    export SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL=0
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_WAR_BARRIER=1
    export SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1
    export SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO=torch
    export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_WQA_WKV=0
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_HASH_TOPK=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_OVERLAP_STORE_CACHE=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=False
    export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=False
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
        --page-size 128 \
        --tp-size 4 \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --device npu \
        --attention-backend dsv4 \
        --watchdog-timeout 9000 \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 6688 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.72 \
        --max-running-requests 64 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
        --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \
        --enable-dp-lm-head \
        --disable-radix-cache \
        --attn-dp-size 4 \
        --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
        --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
        --speculative-draft-attention-backend ascend \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
        --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
<
For the complete benchmark data and additional single-node configurations,
see
|model-deployment-best-practices-deepseek_v4_flash-single-node-pd-mixed|.

*model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-multi-node-pd-disaggregation-deployment*
Multi-node PD disaggregation deployment

PD disaggregation splits the prefill and decode stages onto separate nodes,
reducing interference and improving throughput for high-concurrency
scenarios. This scenario is already covered in the best practice. For the
complete, optimized deployment commands and benchmark data, see
|model-deployment-best-practices-deepseek_v4_flash-pd-disaggregation|.

        *model-deployment-tutorials-deepseek_v4_flash-functional-verification*
FUNCTIONAL VERIFICATION

After the service is started, you can invoke the model by sending a prompt:

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   HOST: the server host address (e.g., localhost)
    #   PORT: the server port number (e.g., 6688)
    # ============================================================

    curl http://${HOST}:${PORT}/v1/chat/completions \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{
            "model": "deepseek-v4-flash",
            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]
        }'
<
Expected result: an HTTP 200 response with the generated text containing
“Paris”.

Once the server prints `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` in the
logs, it is ready to accept requests. For more testing examples (Health

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
GLM-5.1                            *sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1*

INTRODUCTION                 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-introduction*

GLM-5.1 is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model developed by
Z.ai, featuring 744B total parameters with 40B active parameters. It uses
256 routed experts (top-8) plus one shared expert, with Multi-head Latent
Attention (MLA) and DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), and a built-in
multi-token prediction (MTP) head for speculative decoding. The model
features built-in bilingual (Chinese-English) capabilities with a unified
pre-training framework, excelling at reasoning, math, code, and tool calling
tasks. GLM-5.1 supports both Thinking mode (step-by-step reasoning) and
Instruct mode (direct response), with a native context window of
approximately 200k tokens.

This document demonstrates the deployment of GLM-5.1 on Ascend NPUs using
SGLang, including multi-node PD mixed mode, multi-node PD disaggregation
mode, feature configuration, and performance optimization.

This document is validated and written based on SGLang v0.5.16. The current
model (GLM-5.1) is fully supported in this version. To use the latest
features (e.g., speculative decoding, multi-node deployment), it is
recommended to use v0.5.16 or a later version.

SUPPORTED FEATURES     *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-supported-features*

Feature               Example usage
--------------------  --------------------------------------------------------
Tensor Parallelism    --tp-size 16
Data Parallelism      --dp-size 16
Expert Parallelism    --ep-size 16 \--moe-a2a-backend deepep \--deepep-mode
                      auto
Context Parallelism   --enable-prefill-cp \--cp-strategy zigzag
                      \--attn-cp-size 4
PD Disaggregation     --disaggregation-mode prefill
                      \--disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend
Quantization          --quantization modelslim
Chunked Prefill       auto based on device memory, or set explicit
                      value;disable with --chunked-prefill-size -1; e.g.,
                      --chunked-prefill-size 16384
NPU Graph             enabled by default; disable with
                      --disable-decode-cuda-graph
                      --disable-prefill-cuda-graph;control range via
                      --cuda-graph-bs-decode or --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode;
                      e.g., --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 3 4 5 6
Speculative Decoding  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \--speculative-num-steps 3
                      \--speculative-eagle-topk 1
                      \--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
                      \--speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant
Overlap Schedule      export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
DP LM Head            --enable-dp-lm-head

  Note: ~

  The values in the Example usage column are for illustration only. Adjust
  them according to your hardware, deployment mode, and workload. For
  parameter details, see
  |ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning-parameter-reference|; for
  recommended configurations for each deployment scenario, see
  |model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-best-practices|.

For feature compatibility and conflict information between features, see
|ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning-feature-compatibility|.

PREREQUISITES               *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-prerequisites*

Environment                   *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-environment*

documents below:

- |sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-quick_start| --- the fastest way to
  get started. It walks you through launching the official container image,
  starting the SGLang server, and sending a test request. Recommended if you
  are new to SGLang on Ascend.
- |sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-installation| --- the full
  installation guide. It covers the component version mapping (CANN,

  swap). Use it when you need to install or customize the environment
  instead of using the official image.

Model weights               *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-model-weights*

Before downloading model weights, check the model size to reserve enough
disk space. For multi-node deployment, download the weights to a shared
directory accessible to all nodes.

- GLM-5.1 https://www.modelscope.cn/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-5.1 (BF16, 1.51TB)
- GLM-5.1-w4a8 https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.1-w4a8
  (Quantized version, 420.17GB)
- You can use msmodelslim https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim to quantize
  the model naively.

  Info: ~

  We recommend deploying the W4A8 variant for reduced resource usage and
  higher throughput. It (420.17GB) can be deployed on 8 × 64GB of device
  memory (`--tp-size 8`), which corresponds to 8 dies on an A3 Series node
  (4 cards).

This is the minimum recommended configuration. For optimized configurations,
see |model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-best-practices|, which may require
additional cards or nodes.

For the hardware specifications (memory per die and dies per card), see
|ascend-npus-reference-glossary-hardware|.

  Warning: ~

  Ensure sufficient disk space before pulling images. The Docker image
  requires at least 30GB of free space.

integrated into a Docker image and uploaded to the online platform. You can

Both stable releases and daily builds are available. CANN 9.1.0 has no
stable release yet, so the following command uses the validated build tag
`cann9.1.0-a3-B105`. For details, see

[Command]Command

>sh
    docker pull swr.cn-southwest-2.myhuaweicloud.com/base_image/dockerhub/lmsysorg/sglang:cann9.1.0-a3-B105

    docker run -itd --shm-size=16g --name ${NAME} \
    --privileged=true --net=host \
    -v /var/queue_schedule:/var/queue_schedule \
    -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
    -v /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/sbin \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
    -v /usr/local/Ascend/firmware:/usr/local/Ascend/firmware \
    --device=/dev/davinci0:/dev/davinci0  \
    --device=/dev/davinci1:/dev/davinci1  \
    --device=/dev/davinci2:/dev/davinci2  \
    --device=/dev/davinci3:/dev/davinci3  \
    --device=/dev/davinci4:/dev/davinci4  \
    --device=/dev/davinci5:/dev/davinci5  \
    --device=/dev/davinci6:/dev/davinci6  \
    --device=/dev/davinci7:/dev/davinci7  \

  Tip: ~

    default name.

           *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-multi-node-pd-mixed-deployment*

nodes using tensor parallelism while keeping prefill and decode on the same
nodes (PD mixed mode), suitable for scenarios that need more device memory
than a single node can provide. This scenario is already covered in the best
practice. For the complete, optimized deployment commands and benchmark
data, see |model-deployment-best-practices-glm_5_1-multi-node-pd-mixed|.

  *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_1-multi-node-pd-disaggregation-deployment*

reducing interference and improving throughput for high-concurrency
scenarios. This scenario is already covered in the best practice. For the
complete, optimized deployment commands and benchmark data, see
|model-deployment-best-practices-glm_5_1-pd-disaggregation|.

GLM-5.2                            *sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2*

INTRODUCTION                 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2-introduction*

GLM-5.2 is a large language model in the GLM (General Language Model)
series, jointly developed by the KEG Laboratory of Tsinghua University and
Zhipu AI. GLM-5.2 adopts the DeepSeek-V3/V3.2 architecture, including
DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) and multi-token prediction (MTP), and
supports high-throughput inference with SGLang on Ascend NPUs.

This document demonstrates the deployment of GLM-5.2 on Ascend NPUs using
SGLang, including single-node deployment, multi-node deployment,
prefill-decode disaggregation, feature configuration, and performance
optimization.

                      --chunked-prefill-size 16384

                      --disable-decode-cuda-graph
                      --disable-prefill-cuda-graph;control range via

Speculative Decoding  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \--speculative-num-steps 3

                *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2-online-service-deployment*
ONLINE SERVICE DEPLOYMENT

                   *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2-single-node-deployment*
Single-node deployment

Quantized GLM-5.2 models can be deployed on one Ascend A3 Series node.
Select the tab for the quantized weights you downloaded, then run the script
to execute online inference.

W8A8                                 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2-w8a8*

Use the `GLM-5.2-w8a8` checkpoint on one A3 Series node.

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    # ============================================================

    # high performance cpu
    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
    # bind cpu
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy
    unset HTTPS_PROXY
    unset HTTP_PROXY
    unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
    # cann
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
    # MTP OVERLAP
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1

    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1000
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    # DEEPEP
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=72
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=1024
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_COMBINE_ENABLE_LONG_SEQ=1
    export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
            --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
            --attention-backend ascend \
            --device npu \
            --tp-size 16 \
            --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 280000 \
            --trust-remote-code \
            --host 127.0.0.1 \
            --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \
            --port 8000 \
            --served-model-name glm-5 \
            --cuda-graph-bs-decode 16 \
            --quantization modelslim \
            --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
            --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4  \
            --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto
<

Use the `GLM-5.2-w4a8` checkpoint on one A3 Series node.

>sh

    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
    export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1000
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_COMBINE_ENABLE_LONG_SEQ=1
    export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
    export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16
    export DEEPEP_HYBRID_DEPLOYMENT=1

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
            --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
            --attention-backend ascend \
            --device npu \
            --tp-size 16 \
            --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
            --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
            --max-prefill-tokens 280000 \
            --trust-remote-code \
            --mem-fraction-static 0.78 \
            --served-model-name GLM-5.2-w4a8 \
            --max-running-requests 16 \
            --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16 \
            --quantization modelslim \
            --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
            --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
            --load-balance-method round_robin \
            --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
<

                    *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2-multi-node-deployment*
Multi-node deployment

Quantized model `GLM-5.2-w8a8` can be deployed on two Ascend A3 Series
nodes.

Modify the IP addresses of the two nodes, then run the same script on both
nodes.

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   IPS: IP addresses of each node in the cluster
    #   IP_MASTER: rank 0 node IP address with port
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    #   HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for HCCL
    #   GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for Gloo
    # ============================================================

    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
    # bind cpu
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy
    unset HTTPS_PROXY
    unset HTTP_PROXY
    unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
    # cann
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
    # MTP OVERLAP
    export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1

    export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1
    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1000
    export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV

    # Run command ifconfig on two nodes, find out which inet addr has same IP with your node IP. That is your public interface, which should be added here
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>

    # DEEPEP
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=72
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=1024
    export DEEPEP_NORMAL_COMBINE_ENABLE_LONG_SEQ=1
    export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1


    IPS=('<your node1 ip>' '<your node2 ip>')
    IP_MASTER="${IPS[0]}:5000"

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights

    LOCAL_HOST1=`hostname -I|awk -F " " '{print$1}'`
    LOCAL_HOST2=`hostname -I|awk -F " " '{print$2}'`
    for i in "${!IPS[@]}";
    do
        if [[ "$LOCAL_HOST1" == "${IPS[$i]}" || "$LOCAL_HOST2" == "${IPS[$i]}" ]];
        then
            echo "${IPS[$i]}"
            python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
            --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
            --attention-backend ascend \
            --device npu \
            --tp-size 32 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $i --dist-init-addr $IP_MASTER \
            --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 131072 \
            --trust-remote-code \
            --host 127.0.0.1 \
            --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
            --port 8000 \
            --served-model-name glm-5 \
            --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \
            --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
            --deepep-mode auto \
            --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
            --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4  \
            --disable-radix-cache
            NODE_RANK=$i
            break
        fi
    done
<

 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_2-prefill-decode-disaggregation-deployment*
Prefill-decode disaggregation deployment

PD disaggregation splits the prefill and decode stages onto separate nodes,
reducing interference and improving throughput for high-concurrency
scenarios.

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL: prefill master IP address with port
    #   P_IP: prefill node IP address
    #   D_IP: decode node IP address
    #   MODEL_PATH: path to the model weights directory
    #   HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for HCCL
    #   GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME: network interface name for Gloo
    # ============================================================

    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

    unset https_proxy
    unset http_proxy
    unset HTTPS_PROXY
    unset HTTP_PROXY
    unset ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    # pd transfer, prefill master IP
    export ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL="tcp://<your prefill ip>:24707"
    export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600

    P_IP=('<your prefill ip>')
    D_IP=('<your decode ip>')

    MODEL_PATH=/path/to/model-weights

    export TRANSFORMERS_VERBOSITY=error

    LOCAL_HOST1=`hostname -I|awk -F " " '{print$1}'`
    LOCAL_HOST2=`hostname -I|awk -F " " '{print$2}'`
    echo "${LOCAL_HOST1}"
    echo "${LOCAL_HOST2}"

    # prefill
    for i in "${!P_IP[@]}";
    do
        if [[ "$LOCAL_HOST1" == "${P_IP[$i]}" || "$LOCAL_HOST2" == "${P_IP[$i]}" ]];
        then
            echo "${P_IP[$i]}"
            export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=72
            export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=1024
            export DEEPEP_NORMAL_COMBINE_ENABLE_LONG_SEQ=1
            export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
            export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2
            export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
            export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>

            # prefill node
            python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL_PATH}  --disaggregation-mode prefill --host ${P_IP[$i]} \
            --port 8000 --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 --trust-remote-code --nnodes 1 --node-rank $i \
            --tp-size 16 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --quantization modelslim \
            --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend --max-running-requests 64 \
            --served-model-name glm-5 --chunked-prefill-size 524288 --max-prefill-tokens 180000 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
            --disable-shared-experts-fusion --disable-decode-cuda-graph --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --dtype bfloat16 \
            --attn-dp-size 4 \
            --load-balance-method round_robin \
            --enable-dp-lm-head --moe-dense-tp 1 \
            --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
            --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2

            # cp
            #--enable-prefill-cp \
            #--cp-strategy zigzag \
            #--attn-cp-size 4 \
            NODE_RANK=$i
            break
        fi
    done

    # decode
    for i in "${!D_IP[@]}";
    do
        if [[ "$LOCAL_HOST1" == "${D_IP[$i]}" || "$LOCAL_HOST2" == "${D_IP[$i]}" ]];
        then
            echo "${D_IP[$i]}"

            export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
            export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=650

            export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
            export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=0

            export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>
            export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=<network-interface>

            export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1

            python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} --disaggregation-mode decode --host ${D_IP[$i]} \
            --port 8003 --trust-remote-code --nnodes 1 --node-rank $i --tp-size 16 --attn-dp-size 16 --ep-size 16 \
            --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 128 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --quantization modelslim \
            --served-model-name glm-5 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency \
            --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4 --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend --watchdog-timeout 9000 --context-length 180000 \
            --tokenizer-worker-num 4 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --dtype bfloat16  --load-balance-method round_robin \
            --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
            --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
            NODE_RANK=$i
            break
        fi
    done
<
Launch the router after the prefill and decode services are ready.

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   P_MASTER_IP: prefill master IP address
    #   D_MASTER_IP: decode master IP address
    #   ROUTER_HOST_IP: router node IP address
    # ============================================================

    P_MASTER_IP="<your prefill ip>"
    D_MASTER_IP="<your decode ip>"
    ROUTER_HOST_IP="<your router ip>"

    sgl-router \
    --model-id glm-5 \
    --no-tokenizer \
    --policy round_robin \
    --worker-urls http://${P_MASTER_IP}:8000 http://${D_MASTER_IP}:8003 \
    --host ${ROUTER_HOST_IP} \
    --port 6688
<

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
GLM-5.3                            *sglang-model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3*

INTRODUCTION                 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-introduction*

GLM-5.3 is a large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model in the GLM
(General Language Model) series, developed by Zhipu AI. It uses DeepSeek
Sparse Attention (DSA), supports multi-token prediction (MTP), and is
designed for long-context text generation. GLM-5.3 is distinct from the
separately released GLM-5.3-Flash model, which uses a hybrid
sparse/linear-attention architecture.

This document demonstrates the deployment of GLM-5.3 on Ascend NPUs using
SGLang, including single-node deployment, multi-node co-located (mixed)
deployment, prefill-decode disaggregation, feature configuration, and
performance optimization. The multi-node and prefill-decode disaggregation
examples use a locally prepared `GLM-5.3-w8a8` checkpoint and a CANN 9.1.0
runtime.

SUPPORTED FEATURES     *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-supported-features*

Feature                      Example usage
---------------------------  -------------------------------------------------
Tensor Parallelism           --tp-size 16 or --tp-size 32
Data Parallelism             --attn-dp-size 16 (mixed) or --attn-dp-size 32
                             (decode)
Expert Parallelism           --ep-size 32 with --moe-a2a-backend deepep and
                             --deepep-mode low_latency
Pipeline Parallelism         --pp-size 4 with
                             SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=18,20,24,16
Prefill Context Parallelism  --attn-cp-size 8 with --enable-prefill-cp and
                             --cp-strategy interleave
PD Disaggregation            --disaggregation-mode prefill / decode with
                             --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend
Quantization                 --quantization modelslim
Chunked Prefill              --chunked-prefill-size 65536 /
                             --max-prefill-tokens 280000 (mixed deployment)
NPU Graph                    --cuda-graph-bs-decode 2 (mixed);
                             --disable-decode-cuda-graph
                             --disable-prefill-cuda-graph (prefill);
                             --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 3 (decode)
Speculative Decoding         --speculative-algorithm NEXTN with
                             --speculative-num-steps 3 and
                             --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
Overlap Schedule             export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
DP LM Head                   --enable-dp-lm-head

  Note: ~

  The values in the Example usage column reflect the deployment scenarios
  described below and are not universal defaults. Some flags require a
  specific SGLang version or model checkpoint. For parameter details, see
  |ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning-parameter-reference|; for
  recommended configurations, see
  |model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-best-practices|.

For feature compatibility and conflict information between features, see
|ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning-feature-compatibility|.

PREREQUISITES               *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-prerequisites*

Environment                   *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-environment*

Before following this tutorial, complete the environment setup in the
documents below:

- |sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-quick_start| --- the fastest way to
  get started. It walks you through launching a container, starting the
  SGLang server, and sending a test request.
- |sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-installation| --- the full
  installation guide. It covers version compatibility (CANN, TorchNPU,
  Triton, kernels, etc.), building from source or from a Dockerfile, and
  recommended system settings (CPU power scheme, NUMA, swap).

The mixed and PD disaggregation scripts below require a CANN 9.1.0
environment, the corresponding ATB and customized operator libraries, a
compatible SGLang source checkout, and working inter-node HCCL/Gloo
connectivity. Ensure that all participating nodes use compatible software
versions and can access the model weights. The PD topology additionally
requires the configured MemFabric components.

Model weights               *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-model-weights*

Before downloading model weights, check the model size to reserve enough
disk space. For multi-node deployment, download the weights to a shared
directory accessible to all nodes or distribute an identical checkpoint to
the same local path on every node.

- GLM-5.3-BF16 https://www.modelscope.cn/models/ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3-BF16 (BF16,
  approximately 1.51 TB).
- `GLM-5.3-w8a8` (a locally prepared W8A8 ModelSlim-quantized checkpoint
  used in the scripts below; set `MODEL_PATH` to the actual location). The
  checkpoint size and MTP-weight availability depend on the conversion
  output.
- You can use msmodelslim https://gitcode.com/Ascend/msmodelslim to quantize
  model weights for Ascend devices.

  Info: ~

  The deployment examples below use a W8A8 checkpoint with
  `--quantization modelslim`. The PD disaggregation topology uses two A3
  Series nodes for prefill and two additional A3 nodes for decode. Make sure
  that the checkpoint contains the required MTP weights before enabling
  NEXTN speculative decoding.

For hardware specifications (memory per device, devices per node, and
differences between A2 and A3), see
|ascend-npus-reference-glossary-hardware|.

INSTALLATION                 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-installation*

  Warning: ~

  Ensure sufficient disk space before pulling images. A CANN Docker image
  requires at least 30GB of free space. CANN 9.1.0 base images do not by
  themselves include a ready-to-run SGLang environment: install a compatible
  SGLang build, TorchNPU, ATB, custom operators, and other required
  dependencies before running the deployment scripts.

The commands below start CANN 9.1.0 base images. Follow
|sglang-ascend-npus-getting-started-installation| to install SGLang and the
required runtime components inside the container. Use the matching image for
your hardware.

  Tip: ~

                *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-online-service-deployment*
ONLINE SERVICE DEPLOYMENT

                   *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-single-node-deployment*
Single-node deployment

The following single-node example is adapted from the GLM-5.2 tutorial and
is provided as a reference configuration.

>sh
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # Reference only: adapted from the GLM-5.2 tutorial; not yet verified for GLM-5.3.
    # Update MODEL_PATH, SGLANG_ROOT, and the installed custom-op paths as required.
    MODEL_PATH='/path/to/GLM-5.3-w8a8'
    SGLANG_ROOT='/path/to/sglang'

    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1
    unset https_proxy http_proxy HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/opp/vendors/customize/bin/set_env.bash
    export PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_ROOT}/python:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1000
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
    export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1

    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
        --attention-backend ascend --device npu \
        --tp-size 16 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.75 --max-running-requests 32 \
        --served-model-name glm-5 \
        --quantization modelslim --dtype bfloat16 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
        --speculative-num-steps 3 \
        --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
<

                    *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-multi-node-deployment*
Multi-node deployment

For co-located (mixed) serving across two A3 Series nodes, both nodes
participate in a single GLM-5.3 inference instance. The following script is
adapted from the supplied GLM-5.3 W8A8 multi-node configuration, using
TP=32, DP=16, DeepEP `auto`, and NEXTN speculative decoding.

Modify the node IP addresses, model/source paths, and network interface,
then run the same script on both nodes. The two nodes must use the same
compatible runtime and be able to communicate with rank 0 via the
distributed initialization address. In this script, the mixed-serving HTTP
port is 6688 (not 8000).

>sh
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # GLM-5.3 W8A8: two-node co-located (mixed) deployment (A3 Series).
    # Run the same script on both nodes after replacing the variables below.

    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   IPS: IP addresses of two nodes (rank 0 first)
    #   NIC: network interface name for HCCL and Gloo
    #   MODEL_PATH: GLM-5.3 W8A8 weight directory
    #   SGLANG_ROOT: compatible SGLang source checkout
    # ============================================================
    IPS=('<node-0-ip>' '<node-1-ip>')
    NIC='<network-interface>'
    MODEL_PATH='/path/to/GLM-5.3-w8a8'
    SGLANG_ROOT='/path/to/sglang'

    # High-performance CPU settings (requires sufficient permissions).
    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

    unset https_proxy http_proxy HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/opp/vendors/customize/bin/set_env.bash
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/opp/vendors/customize/op_api/lib/:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
    export PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_ROOT}/python:${PYTHONPATH:-}"

    # Keep the allocator configuration disabled as in the supplied script.
    # export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC}"
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC}"
    export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=40
    export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1

    # Optional tuning flags from the original script (disabled by default).
    # export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MLAPO=1
    # export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
    # export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1
    # export SGLANG_USE_AG_AFTER_QLORA=1
    # (and --enable-prefill-delayer on the launch command)

    # Match the configured node IP against all local IPv4 addresses.
    LOCAL_IPS=( $(hostname -I) )
    has_local_ip() {
        local wanted="$1" local_ip
        for local_ip in "${LOCAL_IPS[@]}"; do
            [[ "${wanted}" == "${local_ip}" ]] && return 0
        done
        return 1
    }

    for i in "${!IPS[@]}"; do
        if has_local_ip "${IPS[$i]}"; then
            echo "Starting GLM-5.3 mixed deployment on ${IPS[$i]} (rank ${i})"
            export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2000
            exec python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
                --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
                --attention-backend ascend \
                --device npu \
                --dist-init-addr "${IPS[0]}:5000" \
                --tp-size 32 --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$i" \
                --attn-dp-size 16 \
                --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --max-prefill-tokens 280000 \
                --trust-remote-code \
                --host "${IPS[$i]}" \
                --mem-fraction-static 0.68 \
                --port 6688 \
                --served-model-name glm-5 \
                --cuda-graph-bs-decode 2 \
                --max-running-requests 32 \
                --quantization modelslim \
                --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
                --load-balance-method round_robin \
                --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
                --speculative-num-steps 3 \
                --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
                --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
        fi
    done

    echo "ERROR: Neither IPS address matches this host: ${LOCAL_IPS[*]}" >&2
    exit 1
<

 *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-prefill-decode-disaggregation-deployment*
Prefill-decode disaggregation deployment

PD disaggregation splits the prefill and decode stages onto separate node
groups, reducing interference between long-prompt processing and
autoregressive generation. This configuration uses four A3 Series nodes:

- Prefill group: 2 nodes, `TP=8`, `PP=4`, `DP=1`, and prefill context
  parallelism `CP=8`. It runs DeepEP in `normal` mode and disables NPU graph
  capture.
- Decode group: 2 nodes, `TP=32`, `DP=32`, `EP=32`. It runs DeepEP in
  `low_latency` mode with decode graph capture and NEXTN speculative
  decoding.

Run the following same script on all four nodes. The script selects the role
and node rank by matching a configured IP address against the local network
addresses. Update the model/source paths, the two prefill and two decode IP
addresses, and the HCCL/Gloo interface before running it. The nodes must
reach the prefill master for MemFabric bootstrap and should be started
before the router.

>sh
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # GLM-5.3 W8A8: 2 prefill nodes + 2 decode nodes (A3 Series).
    # Run this same script on all four nodes, after replacing the placeholders below.
    # The IP addresses must match addresses returned by `hostname -I` on each node.

    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   P_IP: two prefill node IP addresses (rank 0 first)
    #   D_IP: two decode node IP addresses (rank 0 first)
    #   NIC: HCCL/Gloo network interface name
    #   MODEL_PATH: local/shared GLM-5.3 W8A8 model directory
    #   SGLANG_ROOT: SGLang source directory
    # Ensure MemFabric, ATB, and CANN 9.1.0 custom ops are installed.
    # ============================================================
    P_IP=('<prefill-node-0-ip>' '<prefill-node-1-ip>')
    D_IP=('<decode-node-0-ip>' '<decode-node-1-ip>')
    NIC='<network-interface>'
    MODEL_PATH='/path/to/GLM-5.3-w8a8'
    SGLANG_ROOT='/path/to/sglang'

    # High-performance CPU configuration (requires sufficient permissions).
    echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
    sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
    sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
    sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
    export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

    unset https_proxy http_proxy HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
    source /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0/opp/vendors/customize/bin/set_env.bash
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/opp/vendors/customize/op_api/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
    export PYTHONPATH="${SGLANG_ROOT}/python:${PYTHONPATH:-}"

    export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
    export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
    export ASCEND_MF_LOG_LEVEL=2
    export ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL="tcp://${P_IP[0]}:24707"
    export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=1200
    export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=1200
    export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC}"
    export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="${NIC}"

    # Test every local interface rather than assuming the relevant IP is first.
    LOCAL_IPS=( $(hostname -I) )
    has_local_ip() {
        local wanted="$1" local_ip
        for local_ip in "${LOCAL_IPS[@]}"; do
            [[ "${wanted}" == "${local_ip}" ]] && return 0
        done
        return 1
    }

    # Prefill: two A3 nodes (32 NPU devices in total); TP=8, PP=4, CP=8.
    for i in "${!P_IP[@]}"; do
        if has_local_ip "${P_IP[$i]}"; then
            export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1200
            export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=72
            export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=1024
            export DEEPEP_NORMAL_COMBINE_ENABLE_LONG_SEQ=1
            export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1
            export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2
            export ENABLE_PROFILING=0
            export SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=18,20,24,16

            exec python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
                --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
                --disaggregation-mode prefill \
                --host "${P_IP[$i]}" --port 8000 \
                --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 8998 \
                --dist-init-addr "${P_IP[0]}:5000" \
                --trust-remote-code --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$i" \
                --mem-fraction-static 0.72 \
                --attention-backend ascend --device npu \
                --quantization modelslim --dtype bfloat16 \
                --tp-size 8 --pp-size 4 --attn-dp-size 1 \
                --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \
     --enable-dp-lm-head \
                --moe-dense-tp 1 --load-balance-method round_robin \
                --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend \
                --max-running-requests 64 \
                --served-model-name glm-5 \
                --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 180000 \
                --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
                --disable-shared-experts-fusion --disable-decode-cuda-graph --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
                --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
                --speculative-num-steps 1 \
                --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
                --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2
        fi
    done

    # Decode: two A3 nodes (32 NPU devices in total); TP=32, DP=32, EP=32.
    for i in "${!D_IP[@]}"; do
        if has_local_ip "${D_IP[$i]}"; then
            export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
            export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=200
            export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16
            export TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=0
            export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1

            exec python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
                --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
                --disaggregation-mode decode \
                --host "${D_IP[$i]}" --port 8003 \
                --trust-remote-code \
                --dist-init-addr "${D_IP[0]}:5000" \
                --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$i" \
                --tp-size 32 --attn-dp-size 32 --ep-size 32 \
                --mem-fraction-static 0.97 --max-running-requests 32 \
                --attention-backend ascend --device npu \
                --quantization modelslim --dtype bfloat16 \
                --served-model-name glm-5 \
                --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode low_latency \
                --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 3 \
                --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend \
                --watchdog-timeout 9000 --context-length 180000 \
                --tokenizer-worker-num 4 \
                --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
                --load-balance-method round_robin \
                --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
                --speculative-num-steps 3 \
                --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
                --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
        fi
    done

    echo "ERROR: None of the P_IP/D_IP addresses matches this host: ${LOCAL_IPS[*]}" >&2
    exit 1
<
Launch the router after the prefill and decode services are ready. The
router example below preserves the GLM-5.2 document's PD routing syntax and
uses the prefill/decode group master addresses.

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   P_MASTER_IP: first prefill node IP (prefill rank 0)
    #   D_MASTER_IP: first decode node IP (decode rank 0)
    #   ROUTER_HOST_IP: router listening IP
    # ============================================================
    P_MASTER_IP="<prefill-node-0-ip>"
    D_MASTER_IP="<decode-node-0-ip>"
    ROUTER_HOST_IP="<router-host-ip>"

    sgl-router \
        --model-id glm-5 \
        --no-tokenizer \
        --policy round_robin \
        --worker-urls http://${P_MASTER_IP}:8000 http://${D_MASTER_IP}:8003 \
        --host "${ROUTER_HOST_IP}" \
        --port 6688
<
  Note: ~

  The prefill and decode groups use separate `--dist-init-addr` endpoints.
  The `ASCEND_MF_STORE_URL` must point to the prefill rank-0 node. The
  `--max-prefill-tokens 180000` and `--context-length 180000` settings
  describe this example configuration, not the model's maximum supported
  context. For troubleshooting, turn off optional overlap or multi-stream
  settings one at a time to isolate compatibility issues.

                  *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-functional-verification*
FUNCTIONAL VERIFICATION

After the service is started, invoke the model by sending a prompt. For PD
disaggregation, use the router address and port `6688`; for single-node
co-located serving, use port `8000`, and for the two-node mixed deployment,
use port `6688`.

>sh
    # ============================================================
    # Before running, update the following variables:
    #   HOST: router/server host IP address
    #   PORT: 6688 for the PD router or mixed deployment; 8000 for single-node mode
    # ============================================================
    HOST="<router-or-server-ip>"
    PORT=6688

    curl http://${HOST}:${PORT}/generate \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{
            "text": "What is the capital of France?",
            "sampling_params": {
                "max_new_tokens": 64,
                "temperature": 0
            }
        }'
<
Expected result: an HTTP 200 response containing the generated answer (for
example, “Paris”).

Once the server prints `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` in the
logs, it is ready to accept requests. For additional testing examples
(Health Check, Generate, Chat Completions, and port usage), see
|ascend-npus-getting-started-installation-testing-the-service|.

BEST PRACTICES             *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-best-practices*

    *model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-best-practice-configuration-reference*
Best practice configuration reference

GLM-5.3 does not have a validated standalone best-practice page in this
tutorial. The |model-deployment-tutorials-glm_5_3-online-service-deployment|
section above includes a four-node PD disaggregation configuration and a
two-node mixed deployment configuration based on supplied GLM-5.3 scripts.
The single-node co-located example remains a GLM-5.2-derived reference. The
configurations have not been independently verified on hardware.

The two-node mixed example uses `TP=32`, `DP=16`, `HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2000`, and
`--cuda-graph-bs-decode 2`. Disable profiling when measuring uninstrumented
service performance.

For this PD disaggregation configuration, prefill prioritizes long sequences
using pipeline/context parallelism and DeepEP `normal`, while decode
prioritizes low latency using DP/EP, DeepEP `low_latency`, NPU multi-stream,
and NEXTN. Tune `--mem-fraction-static`, graph capture batch sizes, and
concurrency based on observed HBM usage, TTFT, TPOT, and request throughput.
Check that the weight conversion and MTP settings are compatible.

For the full catalog of optimization features and their parameter and
compatibility details, see
|sglang-ascend-npus-optimization-parameter_tuning|.
