COMMON OPTIONS                       *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-common-options*

Model and runtime                 *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-model-and-runtime*

- `--model-path {MODEL}`: model path or Hugging Face model ID
- `--served-model-name {NAME}`: stable model name exposed by serving APIs.
  Defaults to `--model-id` when set, otherwise `--model-path`.
- `--model-variant {NAME}`: semantic checkpoint variant to load when one
  model repository contains multiple weight partitions. The pipeline maps
  this stable name to the repository layout before loading; for example,
  MiniMax-H3 accepts `fl2va` and `ref2va`, `fl2va+ref2va` to keep both
  transformers in one server and run each request on the one for its task
  (see |diffusion-MiniMax-MiniMax-H3-one-server-for-both-partitions|), or
  `hybrid` with explicit merged transformer weights to serve all three tasks
  (see the |diffusion-MiniMax-MiniMax-H3-singularity-hybrid-weights|). This
  is a server/load-time choice, unlike a request's `task`.
- `--minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path {FILE}`: advanced MiniMax-H3-only inference
  cache. It replaces the checkpoint's AdaLN projection weights with
  precomputed outputs and only accepts requests whose exact FP32 timestep
  plan is included in the cache. It requires unquantized weights and the
  matching model variant.
- `--minimax-h3-adaln-online {true,false}`: rebuild MiniMax-H3 AdaLN outputs
  from the checkpoint on demand instead of keeping the 24.2 GiB of
  `adaln_proj` weights resident. Video schedules may vary; image releases
  retain their fixed PDD schedule. Requires the unquantized native-layout
  checkpoint. Built plans live in a GPU slab with per-plan LRU eviction; the
  optional pinned-host cache lets evicted schedules swap back in over PCIe
  instead of re-reading the checkpoint.
- `--minimax-h3-adaln-plan-width {N}`: widest timestep plan the online slab
  is sized for (Auto: 4 for video, 2 for image; t2va needs 2, fl2va 3).
- `--minimax-h3-adaln-host-cache-gb {GB}`: pinned host memory per rank
  caching built AdaLN plans (Auto: 8 GB, or 0 for image releases whose fixed
  plans all fit on the GPU). Explicit values are preserved; 0 disables the
  tier. A 50-step schedule needs about 0.9 (t2va) / 1.33 (fl2va) / 1.77
  (ref2va) GB; over-capacity plan sets simply recompute. Expert escape
  hatches (GPU slot count, experimental fp32 rebuild) are the
  `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_ADALN_*` environment variables.
- `--model-subfolder {PATH}`: advanced direct override for a component
  subfolder inside the model repository. Prefer `--model-variant` when the
  pipeline exposes semantic routing. If both are supplied, they must resolve
  to the same weight partition.
- `--lora-path {PATH}` and `--lora-nickname {NAME}`: load a LoRA adapter
  from a local path, Hugging Face repo/subfolder, or exact Hub file URL
- `--lora-weight-name {FILE}`: select one adapter file from a repository
  that contains multiple LoRA revisions. The Hub download is filtered to
  that file plus JSON metadata, so unused weights are not downloaded.
- `--lora-alpha {N}`: supply the training alpha when a single-file adapter
  omits both per-layer alpha tensors and `adapter_config.json`. Do not set
  it when the adapter already records alpha metadata.
- PEFT `adapter_config.json` semantics are applied automatically for named
  adapter slots, RSLoRA, and per-layer `alpha_pattern`. Adapters that
  require unsupported auxiliary parameters or runtime behavior, such as
  DoRA, fail before weight injection instead of silently using ordinary LoRA
  math.
- `--lora-merge-mode {auto|merge|dynamic}`: choose how LoRA is applied.
  `auto` normally merges regular weights, but keeps FSDP-sharded weights and
  supported packed weights that cannot merge in place dynamic. It also stays
  dynamic when an estimate shows that merging would round away more than 50%
  of the update's norm, including with multiple adapters. `merge` forces
  merging where supported; `dynamic` applies the active adapters at forward
  time. See |sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-lora-management| to activate
  multiple adapters through the API.
- `--num-gpus {N}`: number of GPUs to use
- `--numa-node {N} [N ...]`: NUMA node for each GPU worker, the i-th value
  for the worker on local GPU i. When unset, each worker binds its CPUs and
  host memory to its GPU's NUMA node on multi-socket hosts, as srt does
  (CPUs only without `CAP_SYS_NICE`); set `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` to turn
  that off. Unbound workers on a two-socket host (e.g. GB200/GB300) can
  drift to the other socket, which slows host-bound steps and makes latency
  vary run to run.
- `--performance-mode {manual|auto|speed|memory}` / `--mode`: preset for
  latency/throughput and memory defaults. `auto` is the default and
  dispatches residency from selected-GPU headroom and workload type: image
  DiTs stay resident above the 45 GiB threshold, while video DiT placement
  remains model-specific. It uses FSDP only for validated DiT-offload
  replacement paths. `speed` keeps `torch.compile` disabled unless a
  model-specific deployment config opts in after validation; pass
  `--enable-torch-compile true` to enable it explicitly. Use `manual` to
  keep performance-related server args under explicit user control. Explicit
  offload, FSDP, and parallelism flags take precedence in all modes.
- `--direct-gpu-weight-loading {true|false}`: opt into direct GPU loading
  for an unquantized, GPU-resident, TP=1 DiT by materializing its complete
  checkpoint state dict on GPU. Compatible tensors become parameter storage
  without another GPU copy, while tensors requiring transforms can still
  need temporary allocations. It is disabled by default; startup time and
  peak GPU memory remain model-dependent, so benchmark the target model
  before deployment. It is incompatible with DiT CPU/layerwise offload and
  FSDP.
- `--tp-size {N}`: tensor parallelism size. Depending on the pipeline, it
  can shard the DiT, one or more encoders, or both.
- `--sp-degree {N}`: sequence parallelism size
- `--dp-size {N}` (alias `--data-parallel-size`): number of data-parallel
  replicas. Each replica is a full copy of the engine on `num_gpus / N` GPUs
  with its own ingress; generation requests round-robin across replicas,
  realtime sessions stick to the replica holding their state, and control
  operations (weights, LoRA, memory occupation, shutdown) apply to every
  replica. Combines with the other parallelism axes
  (`num_gpus = dp × cfg × tp × sp`); monolithic serving only.
- `--ulysses-degree {N}` and `--ring-degree {N}`: USP parallelism controls
- `--kv-gather-degree {N}`: sequence-parallel degree that splits rows inside
  attention and exchanges with one K/V all-gather (queries stay local)
  instead of Ulysses all-to-all. Non-causal attention only; does not compose
  with `--ulysses-degree`/`--ring-degree` yet. When no SP degree is set
  explicitly, `sp_degree=2` defaults to `kv_gather_degree=2` (its
  measured-win zone) and higher degrees default to Ulysses when the DiT's
  attention heads divide by `sp_degree`, and to K/V gather otherwise; under
  that auto assignment, attention calls the gather path cannot take fall
  back to the Ulysses exchange, while an explicit degree fails instead of
  degrading.
- `--enable-cfg-parallel {true|false}`: enable or explicitly disable CFG
  parallelism. Requests that disable CFG remain valid on a CFG-parallel
  server, but extra CFG ranks redundantly recompute the single active
  branch.
- `--encoder-parallel {auto|fold|dp|replicate}`: how native encoders use the
  GPUs in each DiT replica. `auto` TP-folds a native text/image encoder wide
  enough to benefit, selects batch DP for an explicitly supported native
  text encoder when it can engage, and otherwise keeps the existing encoder
  TP layout; `fold` shards native text/image encoders across the full
  replica whenever dimensions allow; `dp` splits a batched encode across
  supported native text encoder copies and composes with encoder TP;
  `replicate` disables folding and batch DP. Encoder collectives never cross
  `--dp-size` replicas. See |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-encoder_parallel|.
- `--warmup-mode {off|request|server}`: control startup warmup for
  `sglang serve`; `off` skips warmup, `request` primes the request path, and
  `server` runs a full synthetic server warmup before serving traffic
- `--enable-torch-compile {true|false}`: compile native diffusion hot paths.
  When no warmup mode is configured, this also enables server warmup so
  first real requests do not pay compile latency.
- `--offload-during-compile {true|false}`: when compile warmup is active,
  temporarily layerwise-offload DiT weights and move resident non-DiT
  components off-device so `max-autotune` fits on tighter-memory GPUs; the
  configured serving residency is restored before real traffic. Skipped
  under existing layerwise offload, Cache-DiT, or FSDP.
- `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph {true|false}`: capture supported DiT
  forwards as breakable CUDA graph segments to reduce launch overhead. Each
  served shape is captured separately at warmup: pass every served
  resolution in `--warmup-resolutions` (and the frame count in
  `--warmup-num-frames` for video), otherwise only the model default shape
  is captured and other shapes run eager. Unset, it is on for
  `LTX2TwoStagePipeline` on LTX-2/LTX-2.3 when CUDA serving on GPUs with at
  least 130 GiB keeps the DiTs resident (server warmup; no torch.compile,
  Cache-DiT, batching, or `--lora-path`; LTX-2.3 in `resident` mode, its
  default on those GPUs). On a model outside the validated list it stays
  enabled with a warning; compare outputs against eager. If the startup
  warmup captures no graph (the model's denoising stage does not use BCG),
  the server warns that it runs eager. Warmup captures graphs only at the
  warmup request's `quality` level (the default `lossless`, or the level set
  with `--warmup-sampling-params '{"quality": ...}'`); requests at another
  level have no captured graph and run eager with their own fusion set.
  VAE-only request-gated paths are unaffected.
- `--bcg-text-buckets {N...}`: prompt-length padding buckets for breakable
  CUDA graph capture/replay reuse.
- `--attention-backend {BACKEND}`: attention backend for native SGLang and
  diffusers pipelines
- `--enable-attention-backend-autotune {true|false}`: for SGLang-native
  pipelines, benchmark compatible attention backends on each layer's first
  sufficiently large input and keep a backend only when it is both
  numerically compatible and measurably faster. Disabled by default and
  currently validated on SM90 and SM12x. Explicit `--attention-backend`,
  component overrides, and model-required backends are never replaced.
- `--component-attention-backends {MAP}`: per-component attention backend
  overrides, for example `text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=fa`. A key may
  carry a `.self` or `.cross` role suffix to override one kind of attention
  only, for example `transformer.cross=fa`
- `--attention-backend-config {CONFIG}`: attention backend configuration as
  a JSON/YAML file path, JSON string, or comma-separated `key=value` pairs.
  See |docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-configuration| for
  backend-specific options.
- `--srt-encoder-url {HTTPADDRESS}`: address of SGLang srt server with AR
  model for GLM-Image like models. See
  |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-models_with_ar|.
- `--srt-encoder-timeout {SECONDS}`: Timeout in seconds for HTTP requests to
  the SGLang encoder server
- `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout {SECONDS}`: TCP connection timeout in
  seconds for SGLang encoder server
- `--scheduler-rpc-timeout {SECONDS}`: optional end-to-end deadline for an
  internal scheduler RPC, including scheduler queue time. It is unset by
  default so valid long-running and queued video jobs are not failed by the
  transport layer. Set it only when the deployment requires a bounded
  request deadline; caller cancellation and server shutdown remain effective
  without it. Local shared-memory reply files are cleaned up when the RPC
  completes, fails, or is cancelled; timing out does not abort GPU work
  already in flight. A hard process kill cannot run this cleanup, so isolate
  `/dev/shm` per deployment rather than sharing it across unrelated
  services.
- `--request-time-limit {SECONDS|TASK=SECONDS} ...`: mark the server
  unhealthy when a request executes past its limit, queue time excluded. Off
  by default. See |sglang-diffusion-api-cli-request-time-limit|.
- `--sleep-on-idle`: reduce idle scheduler CPU usage by waiting for socket
  events. Disabled by default, matching SRT, to minimize idle-to-active
  wake-up latency. Applies only to monolithic serving with one rank per DP
  replica; TP/SP/CFG multi-rank replicas keep polling. Each wait ends when a
  message arrives, a pending allocator-cache release is due, or one second
  elapses. Active generation is unchanged; benchmark low-QPS tail latency
  before enabling it in latency-sensitive deployments.
- `--enable-trace`: export OpenTelemetry traces for the diffusion scheduler
  and worker stages.
- `--otlp-traces-endpoint {HOST:PORT}`: OTLP collector endpoint used with
  `--enable-trace` (default: `localhost:4317`).
- `--otlp-service-name {NAME}`: `service.name` attached to exported traces.
  Resolution order is this flag, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, then
  `sglang-diffusion`.
- `--enable-metrics`: expose Prometheus metrics at `/metrics` (default:
  disabled). Includes request counts, queue time, host-side stage timing and
  LoRA state, separated by role and DP replica. See
  |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-production_metrics| for metric semantics and
  disaggregated scraping.
- `--pe-server-url {HTTPADDRESS}`: url of SGLang server hosting the PE model
  (e.g., for ERNIE-Image). See
  |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-models_with_pe|.
- `--prompt-enhancer-config {JSON_FILE}`: configure an independent SRT
  LLM/VLM for opt-in HTTP prompt rewriting. Requests use
  `enhance_prompt=true`; no enhancer runs by default. See
  |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-models_with_pe|.

Keep internal scheduler ports on a trusted network: they use Python pickle,
not an authenticated public API. On a monolithic scheduler, malformed
payloads in valid request envelopes receive an error without discarding
other requests received in the same poll. This isolation does not make
untrusted pickle safe or recover from GPU failures.

Disaggregated serving         *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-disaggregated-serving*

- `--disagg-role {monolithic|encoder|prompt_encoder|image_encoder|denoiser|decoder|server}`:
  select the stages run by this process. `monolithic` is the default; the
  split `prompt_encoder` and `image_encoder` roles currently support FLUX.3
  Image.
- `--disagg-server-addr {TCP_ENDPOINT}`: head scheduler endpoint used by
  workers for registration and result routing.
- `--encoder-urls {ENDPOINTS}`: combined encoder pool on the head. For split
  encoding, replace it with both `--prompt-encoder-urls` and
  `--image-encoder-urls`; do not mix the two topologies.
- `--denoiser-urls {ENDPOINTS}` and `--decoder-urls {ENDPOINTS}`: downstream
  worker pools on the head. Each pool URL flag accepts a quoted,
  semicolon-separated list of TCP endpoints.
- `--disagg-p2p-hostname {HOST}` and `--disagg-ib-device {DEVICE}`: worker
  address and optional RDMA device for tensor transfers. The advertised
  worker address and scheduler port must match its entry in the head's URL
  list.
- `--disagg-transfer-pool-size {BYTES}`: transfer buffer per worker
  (default: 268435456 bytes). Include space for incoming tensors, outgoing
  tensors, and preallocated receive slots.

See |docs-sglang-diffusion-disaggregation-flux3-split-encoding| for
deployment commands, ports, and the validation scope. Generation and editing
still use the existing image APIs; encoding is not exposed as a standalone
API.

Sampling and output             *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-sampling-and-output*

- `--prompt {PROMPT}` and `--negative-prompt {PROMPT}`
- `--image-path {PATH} [{PATH} ...]`: input image(s) for image-to-video or
  image-to-image generation
- `--num-inference-steps {STEPS}` and `--seed {SEED}`
- `--num-outputs-per-prompt {N}` / `--num-outputs {N}`: generate multiple
  outputs for each prompt. A scalar seed expands as `seed + output_index`.
- `--quality {exact,lossless,high}`: cumulative request-level optimization
  tier. `lossless` (default) runs every fast path that keeps the reference
  math and the precision of every operand, moving only where the rounding
  happens; it does not enable quantization, sparsity, caching, or another
  approximate path. `exact` restricts it to the fast paths that reproduce
  the reference's rounding exactly, so output is bit-identical in the same
  environment --- ask for it when a run has to be reproducible. `high`
  includes the complete `lossless` set and may also enable model-owned
  approximate optimizations. `extra-high` is accepted as the former name of
  `lossless`. Separately configured quantization, attention, or caching
  options still apply. Support and validation constraints are
  model-specific.
- `skip_softmax_params` (online request only): explicitly enables lossy
  BLASST/Skip-Softmax attention for compatible FA self-attention layers. See
  |docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-request-scoped-skip-softmax|.
- `--height {HEIGHT}`, `--width {WIDTH}`, `--num-frames {N}`, `--fps {FPS}`
- `--output-path {PATH}`, `--output-file-name {NAME}`, `--save-output`,
  `--return-frames` The default image/video filename is independent of the
  prompt and input media name. Set `--output-file-name` when a downstream
  tool needs a predictable filename.

For frame interpolation and upscaling, see
|sglang-sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing|.

Quantization                           *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-quantization*

Component checkpoint paths are selected separately, so changing DiT
precision never silently changes prompt embeddings. The component-scoped
forms are the canonical interface for any component key from
`model_index.json` or a native pipeline's registered module name:

Intent       Canonical option                      Convenience alias           Behavior
-----------  ------------------------------------  --------------------------  ----------------
Replace a    --component-paths.<component>         --<component>-path {MODEL}  Load the
component    {MODEL}                                                           replacement
                                                                               component's
                                                                               configuration
                                                                               and weights
Replace      --component-weights-paths.<component>  --<component>-weights-path  Retain the base
only its     {WEIGHTS}                             {WEIGHTS}                   component
weights                                                                        configuration
                                                                               and replace its
                                                                               weights
Select       --component-precisions.<component>    ---                           Use a
component    {DTYPE}                                                           loader-supported
precision                                                                      exact parameter
                                                                               and execution
                                                                               dtype
Direct-load  --component-direct-gpu-weight-loading.<component>  None                        Use that
an eligible                                                                    component's
component                                                                      audited
                                                                               direct-GPU
                                                                               loader; it must
                                                                               stay resident
Quantize an  --component-quantizations.<component>  --<component>-quantization  Apply a method
unquantized  {METHOD}                              {METHOD}                    supported by
component                                                                      that component's
online                                                                         native loader
Keep         --component-quantization-ignored-layers.<component>  None                        Pass
selected     {PATTERN...}                                                      component-local
component                                                                      ignored-layer
layers                                                                         patterns to its
unquantized                                                                    online quantizer

For example, pair any replacement text-encoder configuration with a separate
single-file checkpoint as follows:

>sh
    --component-paths.text_encoder COMPONENT_REPO_OR_DIRECTORY \
    --component-weights-paths.text_encoder WEIGHTS_FILE_OR_REPO_FILE
<
The transformer-specific `--transformer-weights-path` spelling remains
supported for the primary DiT. Do not mechanically replace it with
`--component-weights-paths.transformer`: the component-scoped form requires
an actual component name, which is pipeline-specific. Use `--quantization`
only to override the method inferred by the transformer loader, and
`--quantization-ignored-layers` to keep matching transformer layers
unquantized during online quantization.

For a native text encoder:

- `--component-paths.text_encoder {MODEL}` replaces the text-encoder
  checkpoint; `--text-encoder-path {MODEL}` is its shorter alias
- `--component-quantizations.text_encoder {METHOD}` applies supported online
  quantization to an unquantized native encoder; pair it with
  `--component-quantization-ignored-layers.text_encoder {PATTERN...}` when
  selected layers must remain unquantized
- Quantization metadata is auto-detected from that checkpoint. The native
  loader accepts compatible serialized formats without a model-name
  allowlist and rejects implementations that do not construct the required
  quantized layers.

The same contract applies to every weighted component: path routing is
generic, while quantized materialization is capability-based. Native
auxiliary loaders whose current materializer expects plain state dicts
reject unsupported quantization metadata before model construction. See
|docs-sglang-diffusion-quantization-quantized-component-repositories| for
the current component matrix. A model cookbook is the source of truth for
published, model-specific checkpoint examples; for example, all H3 sources
and their exact overlays are kept in one
|diffusion-MiniMax-MiniMax-H3-checkpoint-and-adapter-formats|.

Exact precision overrides are capability-based. Native text and image
encoders, standard VAE components, and native plain-state components support
them; other component loaders reject the option instead of accepting a dtype
that their execution stage would not honor.

Direct-GPU loading is also capability-based. The existing
`--direct-gpu-weight-loading` remains the primary DiT path. The component
form currently supports standard native `vae` and `video_vae` state dicts on
CUDA: it streams each safetensors tensor directly to the resident module,
rather than materializing a complete CPU state dict. It rejects custom
Diffusers `auto_map` classes, quantized checkpoints, tied state entries, and
any component-offload or layerwise-offload placement.

Component overrides accept a local component directory, a standalone Hub
repository, or a Hub component subfolder written as `owner/repo/subfolder`.
For transformer and native encoder loaders, an explicit weight filename
keeps the base component configuration and replaces only its weights; the
selected file format must still be supported by that loader.

For supported realtime causal video models,
`--kv-cache-quant {off|int4|int2}` compresses completed KV-cache chunks
independently of transformer weight quantization. It is lossy and disabled
by default.

See |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-realtime_models| for the runtime and model
scope, and |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-quantization| for supported
quantization families and examples.

Request logging                     *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-request-logging*

- `--log-requests`: Log user-facing fields of all requests (default:
  `False`). The verbosity is decided by `--log-requests-level`.
- `--log-requests-level &#123;0|1|2|3&#125;`: Verbosity level for request
  logging (default: `2`). 0: Log metadata (request id). 1: Log metadata and
  sampling config (seed, steps, guidance, resolution, frames, fps, ...). 2:
  Log metadata, sampling config and prompt (truncated to 2 KiB). 3: Log
  metadata, sampling config and full prompt.
- `--log-requests-format &#123;text|json&#125;`: Format for request logging
  (default: `text`). `text` is human-readable; `json` outputs structured
  JSON lines.
- `--log-requests-target &#123;TARGET...&#125;`: Target(s) for request
  logging. Use `stdout` for console output and/or directory path(s) for file
  output. Can specify multiple targets, e.g.,
  `--log-requests-target stdout /my/log/dir`.

CONFIGURATION FILES             *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-configuration-files*

Use `--config` to load JSON or YAML configuration. Command-line flags
override values from the config file.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate --config config.yaml
<
Example:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    model_path: FastVideo/FastHunyuan-diffusers
    prompt: A beautiful woman in a red dress walking down a street
    output_path: outputs/
    num_gpus: 2
    sp_degree: 2
    tp_size: 1
    num_frames: 45
    height: 720
    width: 1280
    num_inference_steps: 6
    seed: 1024
    fps: 24
    precision: bf16
    vae_precision: fp16
    vae_tiling: true
    vae_sp: true
    enable_torch_compile: false
<
HunyuanVideo and FastHunyuan use tiled VAE decode by default so multi-GPU
runs distribute VAE tiles instead of selecting spatial-shard decode. At
HunyuanVideo's supported 960×544×77 shape, spatial-shard decode can consume
99.8 GiB per rank before requesting another 49.61 GiB causal mask. At
FastHunyuan's default 1280×720×125 shape, the mask alone would require
197.75 GiB. You can still override the policy with
`--vae-config.parallel-decode-mode`, but `spatial` and `spatial_shard`
should only be used for smaller validated shapes.

GENERATE                                 *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-generate-2*

`sglang generate` runs a single generation job and exits when the job
finishes.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
      --text-encoder-cpu-offload \
      --pin-cpu-memory \
      --num-gpus 4 \
      --ulysses-degree 2 \
      --ring-degree 2 \
      --prompt "A curious raccoon" \
      --save-output \
      --output-path outputs \
      --output-file-name "a-curious-raccoon.mp4"
<
  Note: ~

  HTTP server-only arguments are ignored by `sglang generate`.

For supported native pipelines, set `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true` to
enable Cache-DiT. It can run with DiT layerwise offload; it cannot run with
FSDP. For the diffusers backend, use
`--backend diffusers --cache-dit-config ...`. See
|sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit|.

Native conditioning reuse is enabled by default, independently of Cache-DiT:

- `--disable-conditioning-cache`: disable cross-request text/image
  conditioning reuse and VAE posterior caching. Reuse within a grouped stage
  remains enabled.
- `--conditioning-cache-max-size-mb {MiB}`: shared CPU and device LRU
  capacity per executor/rank, default `512`; `0` disables cross-request
  caching. Consumed negative text conditioning stays on its original device;
  other entries live on the CPU. The cache bypasses oversized outputs.

See |docs-sglang-diffusion-caching-acceleration-conditioning-cache| for
model coverage, invalidation, and the distinction between cold and
repeated-input latency.

For supported image pipelines, breakable CUDA graph can be enabled with
`--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`, but you must declare every served
resolution in `--warmup-resolutions` so warmup captures matching graph
signatures.

LongCat-Image is supported by this path. Its DiT always consumes a fixed
512-token prompt body, so different prompt lengths reuse the same graph
without model-specific padding. For a 1024x1024 deployment, use:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang serve --model-path meituan-longcat/LongCat-Image \
      --enable-breakable-cuda-graph \
      --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024 \
      --enable-torch-compile false \
      --port 30010
<
SANA-Video supports the same path for fixed-shape serving. Its default text
stage emits a fixed 300-token prompt shape, so the runtime reuses one graph
across prompt lengths without padding it to a generic text bucket. BCG also
requires the serving frame count to match warmup; the example captures the
model's default 81-frame signature:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang serve \
      --model-path Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers \
      --enable-breakable-cuda-graph \
      --warmup-resolutions 832x480 \
      --enable-torch-compile false \
      --port 30010
<

Component Residency             *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-component-residency*

Use `--component-residency COMPONENT=MODE` to assign one runtime residency
mode to each native pipeline component:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers \
      --component-residency all=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=component-offload \
      --prompt "A quiet city street after rain"
<
The available modes are:

- `resident`: keep the complete component on the accelerator.
- `component-offload`: keep the complete component on CPU between uses,
  moving it to the accelerator before each declared use and back to CPU
  afterward.
- `snapshot-offload`: retain CPU parameter storage while a complete
  component runs on GPU. At the end of a use, restore the CPU parameters
  instead of copying GPU weights back. Mutable buffers still move back to
  CPU.
- `layerwise-offload`: keep component weights on CPU and stream its declared
  layers during execution.

Selectors match exact loaded component keys from `model_index.json`,
including names such as `transformer_2`, `audio_vae`, and `connectors`. The
group selectors `dit`, `text_encoder`, `image_encoder`, and `vae` are also
available, together with `all`. An exact key overrides a matching group, and
a group overrides `all`. Components without a matching canonical selector
retain their explicit legacy setting or automatic/model default.

The existing `--dit-cpu-offload`, `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`,
`--image-encoder-cpu-offload`, `--vae-cpu-offload`, and
`--cpu-offload-components` options remain supported. New and legacy options
may be mixed: `--component-residency` wins only for components it matches,
while unmatched legacy settings remain effective. Legacy layerwise selectors
take precedence over legacy component-offload selectors for the same
component. Explicit `--dit-layerwise-offload false` makes the DiT resident
unless another explicit DiT selector, such as `--dit-cpu-offload true` or
`--component-residency dit=component-offload`, selects a different mode.

Explicit component placement also applies during warmup and request cleanup.
Pipeline preferences cannot keep or reload an explicitly offloaded component
merely to prepare for the next request. An explicitly `resident` component
remains resident. This applies to matching exact, group, and `all`
selectors, as well as legacy offload options. Components without an explicit
placement may still use the pipeline's warmup retention and request-end
preload preferences. Selecting one component does not disable those
preferences for other components. On-demand loading and prefetch for
upcoming uses within a request are unchanged; explicit offload may therefore
add weight-transfer latency to the first real request after warmup.

Layerwise selection is strict. A native weighted component selected for
`layerwise-offload` must declare its layer structure; otherwise startup
fails with the unsupported component name instead of silently changing
modes. Explicit non-resident placement also requires a request-time
component-use declaration, so it cannot silently select a module that the
pipeline does not manage. FSDP applies only to resident components. The
Diffusers backend supports only pipeline-wide `all=resident` and
`all=component-offload`.

On NVIDIA CUDA GPUs with separate host and device memory,
`component-offload` preserves existing checkpoint mappings when host
headroom cannot accommodate a weight copy, every parameter is file-backed,
and the dtype already matches. Swap-out restores those CPU views without
weight D2H or a new pinned copy; mutable buffers still return to CPU.
Ordinary, partially mapped, and dtype-converted weights keep the
low-host-memory transfer path, without retaining a CPU weight copy during
GPU execution. Shared-memory GPUs are unchanged. Mapped pages still consume
physical RAM when resident and can count toward a container's memory limit;
avoiding a new host allocation does not mean zero RAM use. When host memory
is sufficient, the normal transfer path remains enabled: its pinned swap-out
storage can make subsequent H2D faster than rereading a mapping. Preserving
mappings is a memory-pressure fallback, not an unconditional latency win.

Breakable CUDA graphs require a resident DiT. Explicit DiT offload with
`--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` is rejected; auto-selected DiT offload
disables graph capture with a warning. Offloading an encoder or VAE does not
impose this restriction.

Snapshot offload                   *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-snapshot-offload*

On NVIDIA CUDA GPUs with separate host and device memory, explicitly select
`--component-residency vae=snapshot-offload` to avoid repeated weight D2H
transfers. Use this explicit mode to retain ordinary CPU weights as well as
checkpoint mappings.

Snapshot offload retains a full host copy during GPU execution. With
`--pin-cpu-memory` enabled (the default), it shares a per-worker host pin
budget with layerwise offload. The budget divides host headroom among
node-local GPU workers. Layerwise initialization claims its allowance first;
snapshot weights use the remainder. Shared parameter storage is pinned once
and reused across requests; its allowance is returned when the storage is
released. Pinning also checks current host headroom, including the cgroup
limit.

Weights that do not fit the budget, or have pinning disabled, retain their
existing CPU storage. Checkpoint mmap stays file-backed unless pinning,
dtype conversion, or weight mutation materializes a copy. Pageable H2D can
be slower, and pinning temporarily needs space for both the original and
pinned storage. This budget limits new pinned weight allocations, not total
process RAM or the CUDA host allocator's cache. Benchmark repeated requests
with the actual host storage and workload; avoiding D2H does not guarantee
an end-to-end speedup.

The whole component must still fit on GPU. Unlike layerwise offload with all
layers retained across denoising steps, snapshot offload does not require a
layer-structure declaration and also covers parameters outside transformer
blocks. Weight updates, LoRA merge/unmerge, and sleep restore the CPU
weights before mutation or release. FSDP-managed components, shared-memory
GPUs, and snapshot-offloaded DiTs with breakable CUDA graphs are not
supported.

Layerwise Offload Tuning   *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-layerwise-offload-tuning*

Use layerwise offload when a component does not fit comfortably in GPU
memory. The compatibility options `--dit-layerwise-offload` and
`--layerwise-offload-components` remain available
(`--layerwise-offload-modules` is an alias), while new deployments can
select the mode directly:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
      --component-residency transformer=layerwise-offload text_encoder=layerwise-offload \
      --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0 \
      --prompt "A quiet city street after rain"
<
Values passed to the compatibility option `--layerwise-offload-components`
must match loaded component keys, such as `transformer`, `text_encoder`,
`image_encoder`, `vae`, `condition_image_encoder`, `spatial_upsampler`, or
`vocoder`. Its `default` group selects text encoders, image encoders, and
VAEs. Use `all` to select every layerwise-offloadable component.

Layerwise tuning options such as `--dit-offload-prefetch-size`,
`--dit-layerwise-resident-layers`, `--dit-layerwise-residency-policy`, and
`--dit-layerwise-residency-lifetime` continue to control the streamed layer
working set. Prefer the smallest component set that solves the memory issue
because layerwise offload can increase latency. DiT layerwise offload can
run with Cache-DiT: skipped blocks are not streamed, and the first layer
after a skip may sync-load. Cache-DiT remains incompatible with FSDP.

Those four set the default for every streamed component. To give one
component its own values, use the `component=value` forms, which also accept
JSON:

>sh
    sglang serve --model-path <MODEL> \
      --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \
      --layerwise-prefetch-size text_encoder=2 \
      --layerwise-resident-layers transformer=4 \
      --layerwise-residency-policy transformer=strided \
      --layerwise-residency-lifetime transformer=permanent
<
The `component=value` maps take the loaded component's name ---
`transformer`, `text_encoder`, `video_vae` --- not a group alias:
`--layerwise-offload-components` understands `dit`, but
`--layerwise-resident-layers dit=4` matches no component and is silently
ignored.

- `--layerwise-prefetch-size`: how many layers to fetch ahead. Fractional
  values are a share of the stack, `>= 1` an absolute count. Deeper prefetch
  overlaps more of the transfer with compute, at the cost of staging
  buffers.
- `--layerwise-resident-layers`: how many layers stay on the GPU instead of
  being streamed. Fractional values are a share of the stack. Resident
  layers pay for a component that runs its layers many times per request ---
  a DiT across the denoise steps, a video VAE across the latent chunks ---
  and do nothing for one that runs them once per request, such as a text
  encoder.
- `--layerwise-residency-policy`: `leading` keeps the first layers,
  `strided` spreads them across the stack so the transfers do not arrive as
  one burst.
- `--layerwise-residency-lifetime`: how long the resident layers stay.
  `forward` (default) places them when the component starts running its
  layers for a request and releases them when it finishes, so they are
  transferred once per request and keep a copy in host memory. `permanent`
  places them at load time, keeps no host copy, and never releases them: one
  transfer for the life of the server.

A component without an entry keeps the group default, so adding these
options changes nothing until one is set. All of these trade VRAM for
transfer. The lifetime decides whose VRAM: with `forward`, only the
component that is running holds its resident layers, so the peak is the
largest single component's set; with `permanent`, every component's resident
layers are on the GPU at once, so the peak is their sum. Pick `permanent`
when that sum fits alongside the activations --- it also frees the pinned
host memory the copies would have held --- and `forward` when it does not.
Measure before raising any of them.

SERVE                                       *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-serve-2*

`sglang serve` starts the HTTP server and keeps the model loaded for
repeated requests.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang serve \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers \
      --text-encoder-cpu-offload \
      --pin-cpu-memory \
      --num-gpus 4 \
      --ulysses-degree 2 \
      --ring-degree 2 \
      --port 30010
<

                         *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-asynchronous-output-saving*
Asynchronous output saving

Use `--async-output-save` to overlap output saving with the next request
during native NVIDIA CUDA serving. It is disabled by default. See
|docs-sglang-diffusion-performance-optimization-asynchronous-output-saving|
for an example, eligible requests, and the response latency and memory
tradeoffs.

Graceful shutdown                 *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-graceful-shutdown*

Set `--http-graceful-shutdown-timeout 30` to allow up to 30 seconds for open
HTTP connections and request tasks to finish after shutdown begins. At the
deadline, unfinished HTTP tasks are cancelled, including uploads that have
not sent their complete request body. The default is unset (wait
indefinitely); `0` cancels outstanding HTTP tasks without waiting.

This controls HTTP draining only, not the full process shutdown time or an
inference deadline. Application cleanup and GPU worker teardown can take
longer; allow for them in your orchestrator's termination grace period. It
does not make asynchronous video jobs durable or guarantee that queued jobs
finish before shutdown. Use `--scheduler-rpc-timeout` separately to bound
scheduler reply waits.

Health endpoints                   *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-health-endpoints*

SGLang Diffusion separates process liveness from inference readiness:

Endpoint              Success condition            Recommended use
--------------------  ---------------------------  ---------------------------
GET /liveness         The HTTP server is           Kubernetes liveness probe
                      accepting requests. It
                      remains 200 during server
                      warmup.
GET /health           Server-based synthetic       Startup and readiness
                      warmup has completed,        probes
                      tracked local workers are
                      alive, and the local broker
                      and any disaggregation
                      routing loop are running.
                      Returns 503 otherwise.
GET /health_generate  Compatibility alias for      Existing integrations only
                      /health. It does not
                      currently issue a
                      generation request in
                      SGLang Diffusion.

With `--warmup-mode off` or `--warmup-mode request`, `/health` returns `200`
once the HTTP server starts, provided its local backend is running; those
modes do not promise that compilation or other first-request work has
completed. If server-based warmup fails, the server terminates instead of
reporting ready.

For standard serving (including `--webui`) and locally launched
disaggregated pools, losing any tracked worker makes `/health` return `503`;
`/liveness` continues to report HTTP availability. The same applies when the
local offline broker or disaggregation routing loop exits, even if its
process is still alive. The broker replies to malformed jobs and inference
errors without stopping; an unrecoverable socket receive or send error stops
it and makes the server unready. A local monitor checks these components
once per second, fails outstanding scheduler requests, and rejects new POST
requests with `503`, even without an RPC timeout. Completed job status and
content remain readable until the server stops. Remove the instance from
routing and restart the whole server; workers and in-flight jobs are not
automatically recovered.

An allocator OOM during a multi-rank forward terminates the affected worker:
other ranks may still be inside collectives, so continuing the next request
is unsafe. Single-GPU replicas, including independent DP replicas, retain
normal request-level OOM handling. The monitor does not detect arbitrary
hangs (see |sglang-diffusion-api-cli-request-time-limit| for requests that
stop making progress), unusable CUDA contexts, or workers on other machines.
A standalone disaggregation router does not own remote worker processes and
cannot validate their health through this check; it only validates its own
routing loop and broker.

Do not use `/health` as a liveness probe: a long server warmup can
legitimately keep it at `503` for several minutes.

Request time limit               *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-request-time-limit*

A hung kernel or collective blocks the workers without logging anything, and
the worker processes stay alive, so `/health` keeps returning `200`. Set
`--request-time-limit 120` to mark the server unhealthy when a request
executes for more than 120 seconds. Time spent queued behind other requests
does not count, and warmup requests are not timed. A `TASK=SECONDS` entry
limits one task of a model that names its request tasks (MiniMax-H3: `t2va`,
`fl2va`, `ref2va`) and can follow a limit for everything else:
`--request-time-limit 90 ref2va=120`. The limit is off by default and is not
available with disaggregated roles.

When a request passes its limit, the server logs the request id, task, stage
and denoising step, asks every local worker to write the Python stacks of
all its threads to stderr, and takes the path of a lost worker: `/health`
returns `503`, outstanding scheduler requests fail, and new POST requests
are rejected with `503`. The hung request is not aborted; remove the
instance from routing and restart the whole server.
`--scheduler-rpc-timeout` is a different bound: it fails one caller's wait,
queue time included, and leaves `/health` unchanged.

Cloud Storage                         *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-cloud-storage*

SGLang Diffusion can upload generated images and videos to S3-compatible
object storage after generation.

On AWS, assign the serving workload an IAM role scoped to its output bucket.
Leave both SGLang credential variables unset so Boto3
https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/guide/credentials.html
can obtain and refresh the role's temporary credentials.

The video exporter and MiniMax H3 launch their local FFmpeg/FFprobe
processes with executable and library paths, locale, temporary-directory,
device and thread settings. They do not copy arbitrary service environment
variables into these children. Custom codec wrappers should not depend on
storage credentials. This is not a sandbox: use separate identities and
filesystem and network restrictions for workloads that do not trust each
other. Third-party libraries that launch their own processes are outside
this guarantee.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    export SGLANG_CLOUD_STORAGE_TYPE=s3
    export SGLANG_S3_BUCKET_NAME=my-bucket
<
For an S3-compatible service such as MinIO, set `SGLANG_S3_ENDPOINT_URL`. If
the service requires an explicit key pair, supply `SGLANG_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
and `SGLANG_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` through your deployment's secret manager.
See |sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-environment_variables| for all options.

The returned object URL is not presigned. For private outputs, keep the
bucket private and authorize downloads separately from the uploader.

Cancellation waits for active uploads to finish before request cleanup can
remove their source files. Allow for the storage SDK's timeouts and retries
in your shutdown grace period. Cancellation does not roll back objects
already uploaded; use your bucket's lifecycle rules for object retention.

COMPONENT PATH OVERRIDES   *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-component-path-overrides*

Override individual pipeline components such as `vae`, `transformer`, or
`text_encoder` with `--<component>-path`.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang serve \
      --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev \
      --vae-path fal/FLUX.2-Tiny-AutoEncoder
<
The component key must match a key in the model's `model_index.json` or a
native pipeline's registered module name. The path must be either a Hugging
Face repo ID or a complete component directory.

Path selection and quantized checkpoint support are separate capabilities. A
pre-quantized component repo must carry its quantization metadata, and the
selected loader must support that serialized format. Native plain-state
loaders fail closed; library-managed components inherit the corresponding
Transformers or Diffusers support. The transformer-specific `--quantization`
flag does not select the format of component checkpoints; their own metadata
does. See
|docs-sglang-diffusion-quantization-quantized-component-repositories|.

              *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-component-attention-backend-overrides*
COMPONENT ATTENTION BACKEND OVERRIDES

Use `--component-attention-backends` when one pipeline component needs a
different native attention backend from the global `--attention-backend`.

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Lightricks/LTX-2.3 \
      --attention-backend fa \
      --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa
<
The component key must match a pipeline module key such as `text_encoder`,
`text_encoder_2`, `transformer`, `transformer_2`, or `connectors`. Component
overrides take precedence over the global `--attention-backend` while that
component is being constructed and fail if the component cannot satisfy
them. A native component may explicitly defer backend selection until first
use; components with fixed attention reject the override. Sparse
self-attention backends use a compatible dense backend for cross-attention
layers. The global backend remains strict for DiT components, while
auxiliary components may fall back to a compatible backend. The Diffusers
backend supports only the global backend passthrough.

You can also pass dotted CLI entries:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --component-attention-backends.text_encoder torch_sdpa \
      --component-attention-backends.transformer fa
<
A component key may end in `.self` or `.cross` to override one kind of
attention only. This helps when a backend's per-call overhead pays off for
self-attention but not for the lighter cross-attention:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --component-attention-backends.transformer.self sage_attn \
      --component-attention-backends.transformer.cross fa
<
A role override outranks the component-wide backend for layers of that role
and is equally strict: it fails the load if it never reaches a layer of that
role. See |docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-per-role-overrides|.

DIFFUSERS BACKEND                 *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-diffusers-backend*

Use `--backend diffusers` to force vanilla diffusers pipelines when no
native SGLang implementation exists or when a model requires a custom
pipeline class.

Key Options                             *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-key-options*

Argument                  Values                     Description
------------------------  -------------------------  -------------------------
---backend                  auto, sglang, diffusers    Choose native SGLang,
                                                     force native, or force
                                                     diffusers
---attention-backend        flash, _flash_3_hub,       Attention backend for
                          sage, xformers, native     diffusers pipelines
---trust-remote-code        flag                       Required for models with
                                                     custom pipeline classes
---vae-tiling and           flag                       Lower memory usage for
---vae-slicing                                         VAE decode
---dit-precision and        fp16, bf16, fp32           Precision controls
---vae-precision
---enable-torch-compile     flag                       Enable torch.compile
---cache-dit-config         Cache-DiT config for
                          diffusers pipelines

Example                                     *sglang-diffusion-api-cli-example*

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path AIDC-AI/Ovis-Image-7B \
      --backend diffusers \
      --trust-remote-code \
      --attention-backend flash \
      --prompt "A serene Japanese garden with cherry blossoms" \
      --height 1024 \
      --width 1024 \
      --num-inference-steps 30 \
      --save-output \
      --output-path outputs \
      --output-file-name ovis_garden.png
<
For pipeline-specific arguments not exposed in the CLI, pass
`diffusers_kwargs` in a config file.

OpenAI API                            *sglang-sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api*

OpenAI-compatible image and video APIs, SGLang action generation APIs, and
LoRA adapter management.

The SGLang Diffusion server supports image, video, audio, and action
generation. It provides OpenAI-compatible image and video APIs, plus SGLang
extensions for
|sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-action-generation-sglang-extension|, mesh
generation, and LoRA adapter management. Audio output depends on the
selected model's audio/video pipeline; action endpoints are not part of the
OpenAI API standard.

PREREQUISITES                  *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-prerequisites*

- Python 3.11+ if you plan to use the OpenAI Python SDK.

SERVE                                  *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-serve*

Launch the server using the `sglang serve` command.

Start the server            *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-start-the-server*

>sh
    SERVER_ARGS=(
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers
      --served-model-name wan-t2v
      --text-encoder-cpu-offload
      --pin-cpu-memory
      --num-gpus 4
      --ulysses-degree=2
      --ring-degree=2
      --port 30010
    )

    sglang serve "${SERVER_ARGS[@]}"
<
- ---model-path: Path to the model or model ID.
- ---served-model-name: Stable model name exposed by the serving APIs. It
  defaults to `--model-id` when set, otherwise `--model-path`.
- ---port: HTTP port to listen on (default: `30000`).

Served model name          *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-served-model-name*

`--served-model-name` separates the public API identity from the checkpoint
location. This is useful when replicas use different local mount paths or
when a gateway needs one stable model name:

>sh
    sglang serve \
      --model-path /models/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers \
      --served-model-name wan-t2v \
      --port 30010
<
`--model-id` is not a free-form deployment alias: it selects the registered
model configuration for checkpoints whose local path cannot be identified.
`--served-model-name` only controls the name exposed by serving APIs. When
both are set, the served name takes precedence for API responses.

 * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

ENDPOINTS                          *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-endpoints*

Select a request task  *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-select-a-request-task*

`GET /v1/models` reports `task_type` (the configured default) and
`supported_task_types` (the tasks implemented by that configured pipeline).
`GET /model_info` also reports the supported `output_types`. A pipeline may
support image and video output on one server when its implementation and
loaded components provide both paths.

Send the optional SGLang extension `task_type` as a case-insensitive enum
name:

Interface                     Task field                     Output constraint
----------------------------  -----------------------------  -----------------
POST /v1/images/generations   "task_type": "t2i"             Image
JSON
POST /v1/images/edits         -F task_type=i2i               Image
multipart
POST /v1/videos JSON or       "task_type": "i2v" or -F       Video
multipart                     task_type=i2v
OpenAI Python client          extra_body={"task_type":       Selected endpoint
                              "t2i"}
Native Python generate        "task_type": "t2i"             Selected task
sampling parameters
sglang generate               --task-type t2i                Selected task

Choose only a task in the server's advertised set. An unsupported task, a
task with the wrong output type for the endpoint, or missing required
conditioning returns HTTP 400. For example, `i2v` needs image input, while
`v2v` and `f2v` need video input. Model-specific size, frame count, and
reference constraints still apply.

If you omit `task_type`, the server uses the endpoint and supplied inputs to
choose a compatible task, preferring its default when compatible. It asks
for an explicit task if several alternatives remain (for example `v2v`
versus `f2v`). Pipelines with one task keep that task as their default.
Sending a request never changes the server default or subsequent requests.

Prompt enhancement        *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-prompt-enhancement*

Image generation, image edits and video creation accept
`enhance_prompt=true` when the server is configured with
`--prompt-enhancer-config`. An independent SRT service rewrites the prompt
before diffusion runs. The default is `false`; image responses return
`data[].revised_prompt`, and video responses return `revised_prompt`. See
|sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-models_with_pe|.

               *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-model-specific-request-fields*
Model-specific request fields

The image and video request schemas contain only OpenAI fields and stable
SGLang extensions shared across model families. Put model-specific controls
in `extra_body` when using the OpenAI Python client:

[Python]

[Python]Python

>python
    from openai import OpenAI

    client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:30010/v1")
    response = client.images.generate(
        model="ideogram-ai/ideogram-4-nf4",
        prompt="A typeset poster",
        extra_body={"preset": "V4_QUALITY_48"},
    )
<
Raw JSON requests may send these fields at the top level. Multipart video
requests may send individual declared form fields or one JSON object in
`extra_params`. SGLang forwards model-specific extensions only when the
active model declares them, so a field for one model family does not
silently change another model.

Image Generation            *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-image-generation*

The server implements an OpenAI-compatible Images API under the `/v1/images`
namespace.

Create an image

Endpoint: `POST /v1/images/generations`

Request quality              *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-request-quality*

`quality` selects a cumulative request-level optimization tier: `exact`
keeps the selected deployment's reference path and all unconditional
bit-exact replacements, so output is bit-identical to it in the same
environment; `lossless` additionally enables the request-gated DiT/VAE
fusions that keep the reference math and every operand's precision and only
move the rounding; `high` includes the full `lossless` set and may also
enable model-owned sparse, caching, lower-precision, or other approximate
paths. `extra-high` is accepted as the former name of `lossless`. The tier
does not override separately configured quantization, attention, or caching
options. Omit it (or send OpenAI's default `auto`) to keep the `lossless`
runtime default. It is distinct from `output_quality`, which controls only
output-file compression. The same extension is accepted by image edits and
video requests.

Python Example (b64_json response):

[Python]

[Python]Python

>python
    import base64
    from openai import OpenAI

    client = OpenAI(api_key="sk-proj-1234567890", base_url="http://localhost:30010/v1")

    img = client.images.generate(
        prompt="A calico cat playing a piano on stage",
        size="1024x1024",
        n=1,
        response_format="b64_json",
    )

    image_bytes = base64.b64decode(img.data[0].b64_json)
    with open("output.png", "wb") as f:
        f.write(image_bytes)
<
Curl Example:

[curl]

[curl]curl

>sh
    curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:30010/v1/images/generations" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -d '{
            "prompt": "A calico cat playing a piano on stage",
            "size": "1024x1024",
            "n": 1,
            "response_format": "b64_json"
          }'
<
  Note For image generation and edits, `response_format=url` requires a
  persistent output directory or cloud storage. If neither is configured,
  use `b64_json`; requesting a URL returns HTTP 400.

Edit an image

Endpoint: `POST /v1/images/edits`

Send a multipart form with a `prompt` and an input image: upload a file with
`image`, or pass a remote image URL with `url`. Supplying both adds two
inputs. Masked inpainting is not supported: uploading a `mask` returns HTTP
400.

Uploaded filenames are sanitized, and saved uploads are constrained to the
server's upload directory. This also applies to image uploads for video and
mesh generation.

Curl Example (b64_json response):

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:30010/v1/images/edits" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -F "image=@local_input_image.png" \
      -F "prompt=A calico cat playing a piano on stage" \
      -F "size=1024x1024" \
      -F "response_format=b64_json"
<
Curl Example (URL response):

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:30010/v1/images/edits" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -F "image=@local_input_image.png" \
      -F "prompt=A calico cat playing a piano on stage" \
      -F "size=1024x1024" \
      -F "response_format=url"
<
Download image content

Read `data[].url` from the response. A cloud storage URL can be downloaded
directly; resolve a relative URL such as `/v1/images/<IMAGE_ID>/content`
against the server address.

Endpoint: `GET /v1/images/&#123;image_id&#125;/content`

Curl Example:

>sh
    curl -sS -L "http://localhost:30010/v1/images/<IMAGE_ID>/content" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -o output.png
<

            *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-mesh-generation-sglang-extension*
Mesh generation (SGLang extension)

For a mesh-generation model, `POST /v1/meshes` accepts an input image and
returns an asynchronous job. This endpoint is a SGLang extension, not an
OpenAI API.

>sh
    curl -sS http://localhost:30010/v1/meshes \
      -F 'image=@input.png' \
      -F 'output_format=glb'
<
Poll `GET /v1/meshes/{id}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. The
content endpoint, `GET /v1/meshes/{id}/content`, returns 404 until the job
completes successfully; an unfinished or failed export is not downloadable
even if a partial file exists. When cloud storage is enabled, use the
completed job's `url` instead.

Job metadata is process-local and does not survive server restart.
`DELETE /v1/meshes/{id}` removes the record, not the running generation or
its output files. Manage output retention separately.

Video Generation            *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-video-generation*

The server implements a subset of the OpenAI Videos API under the
`/v1/videos` namespace.

With `--input-save-path ""`, uploads use request-owned temporary
directories, removed on rejection or after the background job exits.
Configured input and output directories remain persistent. Cancelling
preparation waits for active CPU preprocessing to finish before cleanup; it
does not abort queued GPU work. With `--output-path ""`, cloud upload must
succeed before a job reports completion.

Create a video (text-to-video)

Endpoint: `POST /v1/videos`

    video = client.videos.create(
        prompt="A calico cat playing a piano on stage",
        size="1280x720"
    )
    print(f"Video ID: {video.id}, Status: {video.status}")
<

[curl]

[curl]curl

>sh
    curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:30010/v1/videos" \

            "prompt": "A calico cat playing a piano on stage",

Create a video (image-to-video)

For I2V or TI2V models (e.g., Wan2.1 I2V, LTX-2.3 two-stage), pass an input
image via multipart form upload or a reference URL.

Curl Example (multipart form upload):

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:30010/v1/videos" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -F "prompt=A cat playing a piano" \
      -F "input_reference=@input_image.png" \
      -F "size=1280x720"
<
Curl Example (reference URL):

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:30010/v1/videos" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -d '{
            "prompt": "A cat playing a piano",
            "reference_url": "https://example.com/input_image.png",
            "size": "1280x720"
          }'
<
  Note: ~

  `size` requests a width and height. Some pipelines align these dimensions
  to their patch grid; see |diffusion-Wan-Wan2.2-4-1-basic-usage| for an
  example. Wan-Animate-2 treats `size` as a pixel-area budget instead: the
  output keeps the reference image's aspect ratio and uses the largest frame
  with at most `width × height` pixels whose sides are multiples of 16, so
  `size=640x800` with a 9:16 reference image yields a 528×944 video. Request
  a budget with the reference image's aspect ratio to get a specific size.
  Wan-Animate-2 also ignores `seconds` and `num_frames`: the output has as
  many frames as the (resampled) reference video, generated in chunks of
  `clip_len` frames; see the |diffusion-Wan-Wan-Animate-2-1-2-defaults|.
  Wan-Animate-2 keeps the reference video's audio track on the output; the
  model-specific `enable_audio` field (form field or `extra_body`, default
  `true`) set to `false` gives a silent output.

MP4 encoding                    *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-mp4-encoding*

`x264_preset` picks the libx264 preset for the returned MP4: `ultrafast`,
`superfast`, `veryfast`, `faster`, `fast` (the default), `medium`, `slow`,
`slower`, `veryslow` or `placebo`. Faster presets finish encoding sooner and
trade file size and fidelity at the same
`output_compression`/`output_quality`. Send it at the top level of a JSON
body or as a multipart form field; `sglang generate` takes `--x264-preset`.

List videos

Endpoint: `GET /v1/videos`

Returns up to 20 jobs by default. Set `limit` from 1 to 100 and `order` to
`asc` or `desc` (default). Responses include `first_id`, `last_id`, and
`has_more`; pass `after=last_id` to fetch the next page. The same pagination
contract applies to `GET /v1/meshes`. Pagination bounds each response, not
the number of stored jobs or queued generation requests.

Python Example:

[Python]

[Python]Python

>python
    for item in client.videos.list(limit=20):
        print(item.id, item.status)
<
Curl Example:

[curl]

[curl]curl

>sh
    curl -sS -X GET "http://localhost:30010/v1/videos" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890"
<
Retrieve a video

Endpoint: `GET /v1/videos/&#123;video_id&#125;`

A job is `queued` until the scheduler starts it, then `in_progress`, then
`completed` or `failed`. `progress` estimates denoising progress and stays
below 100 until the output is ready. Multiple denoising stages, including
refinement, share the progress range equally. This is not an elapsed-time
estimate or a measurement of GPU completion.

Progress updates are best effort and never block generation. They currently
support single-node, monolithic serving; other deployments may remain
`queued` at 0 until completion. Job metadata is process-local and does not
survive an HTTP server restart.

When load balancing independent HTTP servers, route polling and content
requests to the server that accepted the job. Scheduler DP replicas behind
one HTTP server share its job store; independent HTTP servers do not.
Restart recovery, durable job ownership, and queue admission limits require
an external serving layer.

An accepted job continues after the submitting client disconnects. For a
bounded scheduler wait, set `--scheduler-rpc-timeout` in seconds; it
includes queue time and generation. A timeout marks the job failed but does
not cancel GPU work. On supported deployments, delete the job to request
cancellation. Retrying generation creates another job, so retain and poll
the returned ID.

`DELETE /v1/videos/&#123;video_id&#125;` removes the API record and requests
cancellation: a cancelled queued job does not start. Running jobs check at
stage boundaries and between sampling steps, independently of progress
reporting. All ranks of a replica stop together. If cancellation arrives
during encoding or decoding, that stage may finish, but subsequent stages
are skipped once the request is observed. Rank-only stages check at executor
boundaries, not inside their sampling loops. There is also a check before
output finalization is started or handed to a background thread. Already
submitted GPU kernels and ongoing saves or uploads are not interrupted; the
API does not return deleted jobs. Cancelled jobs are excluded before dynamic
batching. Once a batch starts, it runs to the end unless every member is
cancelled.

If a replica's cancellation channel is not connected or its queue is full,
DELETE returns `503` with `Retry-After: 1`. The job record remains
available; retry DELETE with the same video ID. A successful DELETE enqueues
the command, not an acknowledgement that GPU work has already stopped.
Cancellation is best effort: process failures or eviction from the driver's
bounded history (the latest 4096 cancelled job IDs) can still prevent it.
Cancellation supports single-node, monolithic serving only; in other
deployments DELETE removes the API record without stopping GPU work.
Completed jobs can be deleted without a cancellation channel. Deleting a job
does not remove files that were already generated. Manage output retention
separately.

Python Example:

[Python]

[Python]Python

>python
    video = client.videos.retrieve(video_id)
    print(video.status, video.progress)
<
Curl Example:

[curl]

[curl]curl

>sh
    curl -sS -X GET "http://localhost:30010/v1/videos/<VIDEO_ID>" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890"
<
Download video content

Endpoint: `GET /v1/videos/&#123;video_id&#125;/content`

Python Example:

[Python]

[Python]Python

>python
    import time

    # Poll for completion
    while True:
        item = client.videos.retrieve(video_id)
        if item.status == "completed":
            break
        if item.status == "failed":
            raise RuntimeError(item.error)
        time.sleep(5)

    # Download content
    resp = client.videos.download_content(video_id=video_id)
    with open("output.mp4", "wb") as f:
        f.write(resp.read())
<
Curl Example:

[curl]

[curl]curl

>sh
    curl -sS -L "http://localhost:30010/v1/videos/<VIDEO_ID>/content" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-1234567890" \
      -o output.mp4
<

          *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-action-generation-sglang-extension*
Action generation (SGLang extension)

Action policies use `/v1/actions` rather than the image or video endpoints.
Launch a supported policy with `sglang serve` and use its cookbook recipe
for the observation schema, action layout, and sampling defaults.

Endpoint                      Purpose
----------------------------  ------------------------------------------------
POST /v1/actions/generations  Generate an action chunk synchronously using
                              JSON or msgpack.
GET /v1/actions/metadata      Discover the served policy's observation schema,
                              action shape, defaults, and capabilities.
WS /v1/actions/realtime       Send successive action requests using the
                              msgpack WebSocket protocol.

See the VLA cookbook https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/vla/intro for Pi0.5,
FLUX 3 Action, and Praxis-1 recipes, or
|diffusion-Cosmos-Cosmos3-action-generation| for world-model action
generation. Supported inputs, session behavior, and transports depend on the
policy; consult its metadata and recipe before use.

LoRA Management              *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-lora-management*

The server supports dynamic loading, merging, and unmerging of LoRA
adapters.

Important Notes:

- Mutual Exclusion: Only one LoRA configuration can be active per target at
  a time; that configuration can contain multiple adapters
- Switching: To switch LoRAs, deactivate the current LoRA with
  `unmerge_lora_weights`, then `set` the new one
- Caching: The server caches loaded LoRA weights in memory. Switching back
  to a previously loaded LoRA (same path) has little cost

Set LoRA Adapter

Loads one or more LoRA adapters and applies them to the model. Both static
merge and dynamic execution support multiple adapters on the same target,
with a separate strength for each adapter.

Each adapter must have a complete LoRA A/B pair for at least one layer on
its selected target. Other layers may be unmatched. If any adapter has no
match, the request is rejected and the previous adapters remain active. This
also applies when reusing a cached nickname on a different target.

When `merge_mode` is omitted, the request inherits the server's
`--lora-merge-mode`. The default policy, `auto`, merges regular weights but
uses dynamic LoRA for FSDP-sharded weights, supported quantized or
AMX-packed weights that cannot merge in place, and updates estimated to lose
more than 50% of their norm to merge rounding. These rules also apply to
multiple adapters. Forcing `merge` fails for weights that cannot merge in
place; `dynamic` leaves the base weights unchanged and adds the adapters'
updates during each forward pass.

Endpoint: `POST /v1/set_lora`

Parameters:

- `lora_nickname` (string or list of strings, required): A unique identifier
  for the LoRA adapter(s). Can be a single string or a list of strings for
  multiple LoRAs
- `lora_path` (string or list of strings/None, optional): Path to the
  `.safetensors` file(s) or Hugging Face repo ID(s). Required for the first
  load; optional if re-activating a cached nickname. If a list, must match
  the length of `lora_nickname`
- `target` (string or list of strings, optional): Which transformer(s) to
  apply the LoRA to. If a list, must match the length of `lora_nickname`.
  Valid values:
  - `"all"` (default): Apply to all transformers
  - `"transformer"`: Apply only to the primary transformer (high noise for
    Wan2.2)
  - `"transformer_2"`: Apply only to transformer_2 (low noise for Wan2.2)
  - `"critic"`: Apply only to the critic model
- `strength` (float or list of floats, optional): LoRA strength for static
  merge or dynamic execution, default 1.0. If a list, must match the length
  of `lora_nickname`. Values < 1.0 reduce the effect, values > 1.0 amplify
  the effect
- `merge_mode` (string, optional): `"auto"`, `"merge"` (force static merge),
  or `"dynamic"` (apply LoRA at forward time). If omitted, inherits
  `--lora-merge-mode`

Single LoRA Example:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -X POST http://localhost:30010/v1/set_lora \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
            "lora_nickname": "lora_name",
            "lora_path": "/path/to/lora.safetensors",
            "target": "all",
            "strength": 0.8
          }'
<
Multiple LoRA Example:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -X POST http://localhost:30010/v1/set_lora \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
            "lora_nickname": ["lora_1", "lora_2"],
            "lora_path": ["/path/to/lora1.safetensors", "/path/to/lora2.safetensors"],
            "target": ["transformer", "transformer_2"],
            "strength": [0.8, 1.0]
          }'
<
Multiple Dynamic LoRAs with the Same Target:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    curl -X POST http://localhost:30010/v1/set_lora \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
            "lora_nickname": ["style_lora", "character_lora"],
            "lora_path": ["/path/to/style.safetensors", "/path/to/character.safetensors"],
            "target": "all",
            "strength": [0.7, 0.9],
            "merge_mode": "dynamic"
          }'
<
  Note: ~

  When using multiple LoRAs:

  - All list parameters (`lora_nickname`, `lora_path`, `target`, `strength`)
    must have the same length
  - If `target` or `strength` is a single value, it will be applied to all
    LoRAs
  - Multiple LoRAs applied to the same target are applied in order

Merge LoRA Weights

Manually merges the currently set LoRA weights into the base model.

  Note: ~

  With FSDP-sharded weights, manual merge may require a full-gather and can
  OOM. Use `set_lora` with `merge_mode="auto"` or `"dynamic"` for the
  lower-peak path.

Endpoint: `POST /v1/merge_lora_weights`

Parameters:

- `target` (string, optional): Which transformer(s) to merge. One of “all”
  (default), “transformer”, “transformer_2”, “critic”
- `strength` (float, optional): LoRA strength for merge, default 1.0. Values
  < 1.0 reduce the effect, values > 1.0 amplify the effect

Curl Example:

>sh
    curl -X POST http://localhost:30010/v1/merge_lora_weights \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"strength": 0.8}'
<

to its original state. This must be called before setting a different LoRA.

Endpoint: `POST /v1/unmerge_lora_weights`
