Adjust Output Quality  *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-adjust-output-quality*

The server supports adjusting output quality and compression levels for both
image and video generation through the `output-quality` and
`output-compression` parameters.

Parameters                        *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-parameters*

- `output-quality` (string, optional): Preset quality level that
  automatically sets compression. Default is `"default"`. Valid values:

  - `"maximum"`: Highest quality (100)
  - `"high"`: High quality (90)
  - `"medium"`: Medium quality (55)
  - `"low"`: Lower quality (35)
  - `"default"`: Auto-adjust based on media type (50 for video, 75 for
    image)

- `output-compression` (integer, optional): Direct compression level
  override (0-100). Default is `None`. When provided (not `None`), takes
  precedence over `output-quality`.

  - `0`: Lowest quality, smallest file size
  - `100`: Highest quality, largest file size

Notes                                  *sglang-diffusion-api-openai_api-notes*

- Precedence: When both `output-quality` and `output-compression` are
  provided, `output-compression` takes precedence
- Format Support: Quality settings apply to JPEG, and video formats. PNG is
  lossless: by default it is stored without zlib compression, which encodes
  fastest but keeps files close to the raw pixel size; an
  `output-compression` other than 75 selects zlib level
  `round(output-compression / 100 * 9)` instead
- File Size vs Quality: Lower compression values (or “low” quality preset)
  produce smaller files but may show visible artifacts

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Post-Processing                  *sglang-sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing*

SGLang diffusion supports optional post-processing steps that run after
generation to improve temporal smoothness (frame interpolation) or spatial
resolution (upscaling). These steps are independent of the diffusion model
and can be combined in a single run.

When both are enabled, frame interpolation runs first (increasing the frame
count), then upscaling runs on every frame (increasing the spatial
resolution).

 * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

         *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-frame-interpolation-video-only*
FRAME INTERPOLATION (VIDEO ONLY)

Frame interpolation synthesizes new frames between each pair of consecutive
generated frames, producing smoother motion without re-running the diffusion
model.

The `--frame-interpolation-exp` flag controls how many rounds of
interpolation to apply: each round inserts one new frame into every gap
between adjacent frames, so the output frame count follows the formula:

  (N − 1) × 2^exp + 1

  e.g. 5 original frames with `exp=1` → 4 gaps × 1 new frame + 5 originals =
  9 frames; with `exp=2` → 17 frames.

CLI Arguments             *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-cli-arguments*

Argument                            Description
----------------------------------  ------------------------------------------
---enable-frame-interpolation         Enable frame interpolation. Model weights
                                    are downloaded automatically on first use.
---frame-interpolation-exp {EXP}      Interpolation exponent --- 1 = 2× temporal
                                    resolution, 2 = 4×, etc. (default: 1)
---frame-interpolation-scale {SCALE}  RIFE inference scale; use 0.5 for
                                    high-resolution inputs to save memory
                                    (default: 1.0)
---frame-interpolation-model-path     Local directory or HuggingFace repo ID
{PATH}                              containing RIFE flownet.pkl weights
                                    (default: elfgum/RIFE-4.22.lite,
                                    downloaded automatically)

Supported Models       *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-supported-models*

Frame interpolation uses the RIFE https://github.com/hzwer/Practical-RIFE
(Real-Time Intermediate Flow Estimation) architecture. Only RIFE 4.22.lite
(`IFNet` with 4-scale `IFBlock` backbone) is supported. The network topology
is hard-coded, so custom weights provided via
`--frame-interpolation-model-path` must be a `flownet.pkl` checkpoint that
is compatible with this architecture.

Other RIFE versions (e.g., older `v4.x` variants with different block
counts) or entirely different frame interpolation methods (FILM, AMT, etc.)
are not supported.

Weight                    HuggingFace Repo       Description
------------------------  ---------------------  -----------------------------
RIFE 4.22.lite (default)  elfgum/RIFE-4.22.lite  Lightweight model, downloaded
                                                 automatically on first use

Example                         *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-example*

Generate a 5-frame video and interpolate to 9 frames ((5 − 1) × 2¹ + 1 = 9):

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
      --prompt "A dog running through a park" \
      --num-frames 5 \
      --enable-frame-interpolation \
      --frame-interpolation-exp 1 \
      --save-output
<
 * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

              *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-upscaling-image-and-video*
UPSCALING (IMAGE AND VIDEO)

Upscaling increases the spatial resolution of generated images or video
frames using Real-ESRGAN https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN. The model
weights are downloaded automatically on first use and cached for subsequent
runs.

CLI Arguments           *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-cli-arguments-2*

Argument                      Description
----------------------------  ------------------------------------------------
---enable-upscaling             Enable post-generation upscaling using
                              Real-ESRGAN.
---upscaling-scale {SCALE}      Desired upscaling factor (default: 4). The 4×
                              model is used internally; if a different scale
                              is requested, a bicubic resize is applied after
                              the network output.
---upscaling-model-path {PATH}  Local .pth file, HuggingFace repo ID, or
                              repo_id:filename for Real-ESRGAN weights
                              (default: ai-forever/Real-ESRGAN with
                              RealESRGAN_x4.pth, downloaded automatically).
                              Use the repo_id:filename format to specify a
                              custom weight file from a HuggingFace repo (e.g.
                              my-org/my-esrgan:weights.pth).

Supported Models     *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-supported-models-2*

Upscaling supports two Real-ESRGAN network architectures. The correct
architecture is auto-detected from the checkpoint keys, so you only need to
point `--upscaling-model-path` at a valid `.pth` file:

Architecture     Example Weights                Description
---------------  -----------------------------  ------------------------------
RRDBNet          RealESRGAN_x4plus.pth          Heavier model with higher
                                                quality; best for photos
SRVGGNetCompact  RealESRGAN_x4.pth (default),   Lightweight model; faster
                 realesr-animevideov3.pth,      inference, good for video
                 realesr-general-x4v3.pth

The default weight file is `ai-forever/Real-ESRGAN`
https://huggingface.co/ai-forever/Real-ESRGAN with `RealESRGAN_x4.pth`
(SRVGGNetCompact, 4× native scale).

Other super-resolution models (e.g., SwinIR, HAT, BSRGAN) are not supported
--- only Real-ESRGAN checkpoints using the two architectures above are
compatible.

Examples                       *sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-examples*

Generate a 1024×1024 image and upscale to 4096×4096:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-dev \
      --prompt "A cat sitting on a windowsill" \
      --height 1024 --width 1024 \
      --enable-upscaling \
      --save-output
<
Generate a video and upscale each frame by 4×:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers \
      --prompt "A curious raccoon" \
      --enable-upscaling \
      --upscaling-scale 4 \
      --save-output
<
 * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

*sglang-diffusion-api-post_processing-combining-frame-interpolation-and-upscaling*
COMBINING FRAME INTERPOLATION AND UPSCALING

Frame interpolation and upscaling can be combined in a single run.
Interpolation is applied first (increasing the frame count), then upscaling
is applied to every frame (increasing the spatial resolution).

Example --- generate 5 frames, interpolate to 9 frames, and upscale each
frame by 4×:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers \
      --prompt "A curious raccoon" \
      --num-frames 5 \
      --enable-frame-interpolation \
      --frame-interpolation-exp 1 \
      --enable-upscaling \
      --upscaling-scale 4 \
      --save-output
<

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Attention Backends           *sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends*

Select and configure attention backends for SGLang diffusion pipelines.

This document describes the attention backends available in sglang diffusion
(`sglang.multimodal_gen`) and how to select them.

OVERVIEW                   *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-overview*

Attention backends are defined by `AttentionBackendEnum`
(`sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms.interface.AttentionBackendEnum`)
and selected via the CLI flag `--attention-backend`.

Backend selection is performed by the shared attention layers (e.g.
`LocalAttention` / `USPAttention` / `UlyssesAttention` in
`sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.layers.attention.layer`).
`--attention-backend` is strict for the diffusion transformer / DiT.
Auxiliary components such as encoders and VAEs use it when compatible, then
fall back to a component default or a platform-compatible backend. Use
`--component-attention-backends` when an auxiliary component must use a
specific backend; incompatible overrides, including an override for a
component that constructs no SGLang attention layer, fail unless a sparse
backend is being replaced for cross-attention. A component key may carry a
`.self` or `.cross` role suffix to override just one kind of attention; see
|docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-per-role-overrides|.

When using the diffusers backend, `--attention-backend` is passed through to
diffusers' `set_attention_backend` (e.g., `flash`, `_flash_3_hub`, `sage`,
`xformers`, `native`).

- CUDA: prefers FlashAttention (FA3/FA4) when supported; otherwise falls
  back to PyTorch SDPA. On SM100/SM103 (B200/B300), dense non-causal
  fp16/bf16 native attention prefers cuDNN SDPA and falls back to FA4 if
  cuDNN has no compatible kernel.
- ROCm: on Instinct (CDNA, gfx9) GPUs, defaults to `aiter` when
  `--attention-backend` is not set; on Radeon (RDNA) GPUs, use `torch_sdpa`.
  `aiter_sage`, `aiter_quant` and `torch_sdpa` can be selected explicitly.
  FlashAttention dispatches through FA3, which is CUDA-only, so `fa` falls
  back to PyTorch SDPA on ROCm.
- Intel XPU: uses XPU Flash Attention backend (fp16/bf16, head sizes
  64/96/128/192/256); otherwise falls back to PyTorch SDPA.
- MUSA: uses FlashAttention when available; also supports Sage Attention
  when installed; otherwise falls back to PyTorch SDPA.
- MPS: always uses PyTorch SDPA.
- NPU: for ring attention uses FA otherwise uses PyTorch SDPA.
- CPU: uses `amx_attn` when the CPU supports AMX, the dtype is bf16/fp16,
  and the head size is even; otherwise PyTorch SDPA.

On Blackwell, `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa` keeps FA4 for attention with one side
shorter than 128 tokens and the other at least 128 during breakable CUDA
graph warmup, capture and replay, including the eager breaks of a replay. In
eager execution outside a graph, `lossless` and `high` requests use cuDNN
for these shapes to avoid FA4 host-dispatch overhead; `exact` keeps the
reference FA4 route. Switching backends can change floating-point rounding.

BACKEND OPTIONS     *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-backend-options*

For SGLang-native pipelines, the CLI accepts the lowercase names of
`AttentionBackendEnum`. The table below lists the backends implemented by
the built-in platforms. `fa3`/`fa4` are accepted as aliases for `fa`.

                 *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-selection-priority*
SELECTION PRIORITY

The selection order in `runtime/layers/attention/selector.py` is:

1. `global_force_attn_backend(...)` /
   `global_force_attn_backend_context_manager(...)`
2. Component and role override from
   `--component-attention-backends.<component>.<role>` while that component
   is being constructed
3. Component override from `--component-attention-backends` while that
   component is being constructed
4. CLI `--attention-backend` (`ServerArgs.attention_backend`)
5. Layer or component default, when declared
6. Auto selection (platform capability, dtype, and installed packages)

An explicit global backend mismatch fails for DiT self-attention. Auxiliary
components may fall back to their declared default or another compatible
backend. Sparse backends selected for self-attention similarly fall back to
a compatible dense backend for cross-attention. Explicit component overrides
are otherwise strict.

                 *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-per-role-overrides*
Per-role overrides

A role is the kind of attention a layer performs: `self` or `cross`.
Appending a role to a component key selects a backend for just that role,
which is useful when a quantized or otherwise expensive backend pays off for
self-attention but not for the much lighter cross-attention:

[Command]

[Command]Command

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --component-attention-backends.transformer.self sage_attn \
      --component-attention-backends.transformer.cross fa
<
A role override outranks the component-wide backend for layers of that role
and leaves the other role alone. Layers of a role with no override fall
through to the component-wide backend as usual, and `<component>_2` inherits
`<component>`'s role overrides unless it declares its own.

Role overrides are as strict as component-wide ones: a role override that
never reaches a layer fails the load, including when the component builds no
layers of that role at all. The one tolerated divergence is the shared
sparse rule above --- a sparse backend named for `cross` is replaced by a
compatible dense backend and logged, rather than failing.

Model and layer backend sets guide automatic selection; they are not
positive allowlists for explicit requests. A backend selected with
`--attention-backend` or `--component-attention-backends` can therefore be
used without first adding it to every model's set. It still fails closed
when the platform cannot resolve it or when it lacks a required operation
such as dense cross-attention, packed variable-length attention, or
ring-attention LSE. Model paths that require one backend for correctness
declare it as required; those layers keep that backend even when the
surrounding component is overridden.

For an automatic, measurement-based choice, pass
`--enable-attention-backend-autotune true`. On each layer's first
sufficiently large input, the native runtime times compatible candidates and
switches only when the output remains within its numerical guard and the
measured gain exceeds the noise margin. The tuner is disabled by default and
currently validated on SM90 and SM12x. It does not replace a backend
selected explicitly through `--attention-backend` or
`--component-attention-backends`, or a backend required by the model for
correctness.

CONFIGURATION         *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-configuration*

Some backends require additional configuration. You can pass these
parameters via `--attention-backend-config`. This argument accepts:

- A path to a JSON or YAML configuration file.
- A JSON string (e.g., `'&#123;"sparsity": 0.5&#125;'`).
- Key-value pairs (e.g., `"sparsity=0.5,enable_x=true"`).

The key-value form splits on commas, so list values (for example Sol-Attn
`dense_layers=0,1` or VSA-H3 `vsa_dense_layers`) must use the JSON or file
form, e.g. `'&#123;"dense_layers": "0,1"&#125;'` for Sol-Attn or
`'&#123;"vsa_dense_layers": [0, 1]&#125;'` for VSA-H3 (a JSON list, not a
string). Sol-Attn also accepts ranges such as `dense_layers=0-1`.

 *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-supported-configuration-parameters*
Supported Configuration Parameters

Sliding Tile Attention (`sliding_tile_attn`)

VSA-H3 constraints:

- Only the DiT runs sparse; the token refiner, text encoder, and VAEs keep
  their dense defaults. An explicit
  `--component-attention-backends text_encoder=fa` is rejected because the
  H3 text encoder has SDPA-only layers.
- Uses the checkpoint's trained `to_gate_compress` compression branch. Base
  MiniMax-H3 weights load zero gates and run pure sparse.
- Ulysses sequence parallelism is supported; `--ring-degree` greater than 1,
  `torch.compile`, and breakable CUDA graph execution are rejected.

Hybrid window attention for VDN-H3 (`hybrid_window_attn_h3`)

|diffusion-MiniMax-MiniMax-H3-7-vdn-h3-hybrid-attention-8-step-distill|
replaces every DiT block's dense self-attention with two branches. The
softmax branch is an exact softmax over a chunk-aligned frame window (frame
`t` belongs to chunk `t // 5` and attends to chunks `c - 1 .. c + 1`; frames
0 and F-1 are dense as rows and columns; every text / audio pair stays
dense) scaled by a per-head sigmoid gate. The linear branch (a frame-wise
Video Delta rule recurrence, forward and reverse over frames) covers exactly
the window's complement and is driven by the attention module. The mask is
request-static, so the metadata is built once per request. The checkpoint's
`transformer/config.json` carries the window geometry; the backend reads it.

Parameter            Type  Description                                 Default
-------------------  ----  ------------------------------------------  -------
vdn_h3_dense_smoke   bool  Allows a dense transformer backend (fa) on  false
                           the VDN-H3 weights for the base-H3 + LoRA
                           equivalence smoke. The gates and the
                           linear branch are skipped: a study, not a
                           sample.
vdn_max_gather_rows  int   Upper bound on the gathered K/V rows per    200000
                           window FlashAttention call; consecutive
                           chunk groups fill one call up to it.
                           Splitting changes no query's kept key set,
                           only the pass count and the gather's peak
                           memory.

Hybrid window attention constraints:

- VDN-H3 requires this backend for the transformer; a dense backend on these
  weights would silently skip the linear branch and the gates, so it is
  rejected unless `vdn_h3_dense_smoke` is set. The token refiner, text
  encoder, and VAEs keep dense attention.
- Base MiniMax-H3 and FastH3 checkpoints have no linear branch and are
  rejected by this backend.
- Ulysses sequence parallelism is supported (QK-norm + RoPE run after the
  all-to-all on the head shard); `--ring-degree` greater than 1,
  `torch.compile`, and breakable CUDA graph execution are rejected.

Ascend sparse attention (`ascend_sparse_attn`)

On Linux with Ascend NPUs, install the
|docs-sglang-diffusion-installation-ascend-npu| and a compatible MindIE-SD
https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD/tree/3.2.0 build exposing
`sparse_attention` and the native operators for your selected sparse mode.
Backend loading reports a missing MindIE-SD dependency before model
execution.

Sparse steps use MindIE-SD. Dense steps use the public Laser attention
backend on A2/A3 and Ascend FA backend on A5. Components with causal
attention, grouped query attention, or head sizes unsupported by Laser use
Ascend FA. Sparse and dense precision default to BF16.

For RFv3, FP8 and MXFP4 use a default KV block size of 256 in MindIE-SD. Its
video-span route requires matching Q/KV blocks, so this adapter defaults
`block_size` to 256 for those modes. The public sparse API does not forward
a separate KV block-size override. On A5, MindIE-SD remaps `rf_v2` to
`rf_v3` and rejects `ada_bsa`.

The Ascend FA dense route requires the public metadata API from PR #46029
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46029, including for default BF16
execution. It passes `dense_kwargs` through that metadata class and requires
compatible native operators for the selected precision. Layer layout and
softmax scale remain owned by the attention layer.

Dense option     Accepted values and effect                  Default
---------------  ------------------------------------------  -----------------
precision        bf16, fp8, mxfp8, or mxfp4.                 bf16
fp8_fa_mode      FP8-only mode string, such as               HIGH_PRECISION
                 HIGH_PRECISION or C8V16_TILING512, or JSON
                 null for vendor normalization.
head_chunk_size  Non-negative head chunk size passed to      4
                 Ascend FA. Zero disables head chunking.
qk_rotation      Boolean controlling online Q/K rotation     Ascend FA default
                 for quantized dense attention. Omit it to
                 retain Ascend FA's checkpoint-aware
                 default.

Keep causal components on a backend that preserves their masks. MiniMax-H3
keeps its token refiner on dense FA and defaults its text encoder to SDPA
unless you explicitly override it. Video spans retain their original packed
token positions and are rebased within each independent document. With H3's
explicit trailing-padding contract, attention skips the physical alignment
tail and returns zeros for those rows, including with Ulysses sequence
parallelism.

AITER Quant (`aiter_quant`)

The backend passes raw BF16 Q/K/V to `aiter.ops.mha_v4`, which applies the
canonical quantizer for the requested operand pair and launches the matching
ASM row. No calibration pass and no extra checkpoint weights are involved:
the format is purely a runtime choice.

Parameter  Type  Description                                           Default
---------  ----  ----------------------------------------------------  -------
format     str   Quant format for the mha_v4 call, one of the names    fp8
                 in the table below. An unknown name, or one with no
                 kernel row on the active arch, raises at
                 construction rather than falling back.

Variants, from widest operands to narrowest. Q and K always share an
encoding; only V varies independently.

Variant  Q/K format  V format    Architectures   Description
-------  ----------  ----------  --------------  -----------------------------
bf16fp8  BF16        FP8         gfx950          Quantizes only PV, preserving
                                                 BF16 attention scores for
                                                 conservative quality.
i8fp8    INT8        FP8         gfx950, gfx942  Uniform 8-bit Q/K
                                                 quantization; effective for
                                                 well-conditioned values but
                                                 sensitive to outliers.
fp8      FP8         FP8         gfx950, gfx942  Default native FP8: E4M3 on
                                                 gfx950 and E4M3FNUZ on
                                                 gfx942.
mxfp8    MXFP8 E4M3  FP8         gfx950          Per-1x32 E8M0 Q/K scales and
                                                 a per-tensor V scale improve
                                                 outlier handling.
mxfp6    MXFP6 E2M3  FP8         gfx950          Block-scaled 6-bit Q/K
                                                 balances compression,
                                                 throughput, and quality.
mxfp4    MXFP4 E2M1  MXFP4 E2M1  gfx950          The most compact block-scaled
                                                 Q/K/V format; validate
                                                 quality for the target
                                                 workload.

AITER quant constraints:

- Every row targets full-MHA `head_dim == 128` and non-causal attention; a
  causal layer or another head dim raises rather than falling back. Varlen
  attention is not supported.
- gfx942 ships only the `i8fp8` and `fp8` kernel rows. Every other format is
  gfx950-only and is rejected at construction on gfx942.
- Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and an `aiter` build that ships
  `aiter.ops.mha_v4`.

USAGE                         *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-usage*

           *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-select-a-backend-via-cli*
Select a backend via CLI

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --prompt "..." \
      --attention-backend fa
<
>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --prompt "..." \
      --attention-backend torch_sdpa
<

             *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-override-one-component*
Override one component

Use component overrides when a specific module needs different attention
semantics from the main transformer:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --prompt "..." \
      --attention-backend fa \
      --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa
<
Component keys match pipeline module names from `model_index.json`, such as
`text_encoder`, `text_encoder_2`, `transformer`, `transformer_2`, or
`connectors`. Use this override when the fallback must be pinned: unlike the
global backend, an incompatible component override raises an error instead
of selecting another backend. The one role-based exception is a sparse
self-attention backend, which uses a compatible dense backend for
cross-attention layers in the same component. The component must construct
SGLang-selectable attention or explicitly defer selection until first use;
components with fixed attention reject the override. Per-component overrides
apply only to native pipelines. The Diffusers backend accepts the global
`--attention-backend` passthrough instead.

  *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-per-request-override-denoise-loop*
Per-request override (denoise loop)

A single server can serve exact and approximate attention side by side:
requests may switch the DiT denoise attention backend via the
`attention_backend_override` sampling param. Valid values are the
exact/drop-in dense kernels --- `fa`, `torch_sdpa`, `sage_attn`,
`sage_attn_3`. The field participates in the dynamic-batch signature, so
requests with different backends never share a batch.

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --prompt "..." \
      --attention-backend-override sage_attn
<
>python
    client.images.generate(
        model="<MODEL_PATH_OR_ID>",
        prompt="...",
        extra_body={"attention_backend_override": "sage_attn"},
    )
<
Incompatible server settings reject the request (with a server log) instead
of silently falling back: breakable CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` bake the
attention kernel into a captured/traced graph; sparse server backends
(`sliding_tile_attn`, `video_sparse_attn`, ...) cannot be mixed with
per-request dense switching; under ring parallelism the target must be
ring-capable. Note `sage_attn` / `sage_attn_3` are lossy (quantized
attention) --- validate quality on your workload.

        *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-request-scoped-skip-softmax*
Request-scoped Skip Softmax

Skip Softmax (BLASST) keeps the QK matmul, but skips the exponential,
softmax-state update, V load, and PV matmul for attention tiles whose
estimated softmax mass is below a threshold. It is an explicit lossy
optimization backed by the FlashInfer kernels shipped with SGLang's pinned
dependencies. See the BLASST paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12087 and
NVIDIA's video-generation study
https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/blob/main/docs/source/blogs/tech_blog/blog28_Accelerating_Video_Generation_with_GEMM_Quantization_Attention_Quantization_and_Skip_Softmax_Attention_in_TensorRT-LLM.md
for the algorithm and measured quality/performance trade-offs.

Pass `skip_softmax_params` in one image or video request. The runtime routes
compatible self-attention layers through the FA/FlashInfer path for that
batch; cross-attention keeps its normal backend, and the next request
restores the server default.

>python
    client.videos.create(
        model="<MODEL_PATH_OR_ID>",
        prompt="...",
        extra_body={
            "skip_softmax_params": {
                "threshold_scale_factor": 500.0,
                "start_step": 14,
            }
        },
    )
<
- `threshold_scale_factor` is required and must be positive. The kernel uses
  `threshold_scale_factor / context_length`; larger values skip more work
  and usually increase quality loss.
- `start_step` is the zero-based denoising step at which sparse execution
  starts. It defaults to `0`; keeping early high-noise steps dense is
  generally safer.

There is intentionally no default threshold. Calibrate the threshold and
start step against output-quality metrics for each model, resolution, step
count, and deployment backend; values tuned for one workload are not
portable.

Current support is FP16/BF16, head dimension 128 or 256, and unmasked
self-attention on Hopper SM90 and Blackwell SM100/SM103/SM107. Ulysses
sequence parallelism is supported because the kernel runs after its
all-to-all. Ring Attention, attention masks, `torch.compile`, and breakable
CUDA graphs reject the request instead of silently running dense attention.
Models that merely offer an FA backend do not automatically qualify: the
runtime still checks the GPU, dtype, head dimension, attention role, and
execution mode.

              *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-using-spargeattention*
Using SpargeAttention

Install the optional CUDA extension, then select the backend explicitly:

>sh
    pip install ninja
    pip install git+https://github.com/thu-ml/SpargeAttn.git --no-build-isolation

    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --prompt "..." \
      --attention-backend sparge_attn \
      --attention-backend-config topk=0.5
<
`sparge_attn` applies to compatible self-attention layers. Cross-attention
uses the existing dense fallback; short self-attention and asymmetric Q/KV
also use dense SDPA. LTX-2, LTX-2.3, and LTX-2.5 have compatible video (128)
and audio (64) head dimensions, so their sufficiently long, unmasked
self-attention uses SpargeAttention while prompt and audio-video
cross-attention remain dense. Ulysses sequence parallelism is supported, but
ring attention is not because the upstream kernel does not expose the
softmax LSE needed for ring merging. K/V-gather SP therefore follows the
normal sparse-backend rule and uses Ulysses instead.

               *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-sage-then-sol-hybrid*
Sage then Sol hybrid

`sol_attn` keeps the first `dense_steps` steps dense. Set
`dense_backend=sage_attn` to run that prefix on SageAttention and the tail
on Sol sparse attention. Keep the text encoder on `torch_sdpa`:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
      --model-variant fl2va \
      --attention-backend sol_attn \
      --attention-backend-config dense_backend=sage_attn,dense_steps=10 \
      --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn \
      --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \
      --save-output
<
Both `sage_attn` and `sol_attn` are approximate. The default DiT backend
remains `fa`.

*docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-ascend-quantized-attention-with-mindie-sd*
Ascend quantized attention with MindIE-SD

On Ascend NPU, `fa` can use the public `mindiesd.quant_attention` API for
FP8, MXFP8, and MXFP4 attention. This integration targets MiniMax-H3;
Wan/FLUX support is out of scope. Omitting `precision` preserves the
existing native Ascend FA behavior, including its opt-in MXFP8 path. Set
`precision=bf16` to explicitly select native floating-point attention.
Neither requires MindIE-SD.

When FA is an internal dense fallback for another selected backend, that
backend's `precision` does not enable quantized FA. The denoising stage
passes configuration through `AscendFAMetadata`; the FA constructor does not
read global server arguments. Quantization applies to DiT self-attention. H3
refiners and cross-attention do not inherit its quantized path.

           *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-install-the-optional-sdk*
Install the optional SDK

Use Linux with an Ascend 950 (A5), the CANN toolkit/operator packages, and a
matching Torch/TorchNPU installation. Activate the Python environment that
runs SGLang before building: the SDK's native extension uses that
environment's Torch ABI. Keep the Torch/TorchNPU versions required by your
SGLang checkout; the SDK's root `requirements.txt` pins Torch/TorchNPU 2.9
and must not replace them.

Install the official 3.2.0 wheel
https://pypi.org/project/mindiesd/3.2.0/#files if its Python, architecture,
glibc, and Torch ABI match your environment.

>sh
    python3 -m pip install --no-deps --only-binary=:all: "mindiesd==3.2.0"
<
`--no-deps` preserves the installed Torch/TorchNPU versions.

If no compatible wheel is available, build the `3.2.0` release in a
user-owned directory. The example sets `ASCEND_COMPUTE_UNIT=ascend950` for
quantized FA on Ascend 950. For sparse attention on a supported 910-series
device, set `ASCEND_COMPUTE_UNIT` to the target chip or leave it unset to
use the SDK defaults for your CANN version.

>sh
    # Adjust this path to your CANN installation.
    source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
    git clone --branch 3.2.0 --depth 1 https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD.git
    cd MindIE-SD
    # Release commit: 65bd01133998ab018052fdb6f55dea5a873e584f
    python3 -m pip install "setuptools>=65.5" build wheel "cmake<4.1"

    # 3.2.0 makes build/vendors read-only before the following AICPU copy.
    # Restore owner write permission between those two build steps.
    python3 - <<'PY'
    from pathlib import Path

    path = Path("build/build_ops.sh")
    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    marker = "    sync_aicpu_ops_to_transformer_vendor\n"
    assert source.count(marker) == 1
    source = source.replace(
        marker,
        '    chmod u+w "${current_script_dir}/vendors"\n' + marker,
        1,
    )
    path.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
    PY

    MINDIE_SD_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.2.0 ASCEND_COMPUTE_UNIT=ascend950 \
      python3 -m build --wheel --no-isolation
    python3 -m pip install --no-deps dist/mindiesd-3.2.0-*.whl
<
The release still defaults its package version to `3.1.0`, so the build
command sets the release version explicitly. The permission workaround
addresses the non-root `customize_transformer` directory creation failure in
the release's build script
https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD/blob/3.2.0/build/build_ops.sh. It does
not require root or disable operator builds. You also need the CANN
development toolchain; see the pinned installation guide
https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD/blob/3.2.0/docs/en/installation.md and
build guide
https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD/blob/3.2.0/docs/en/developer_guide/build_guide.md.

Environment                         Validation status
----------------------------------  ------------------------------------------
Ascend 950, Torch/TorchNPU 2.10.0,  H3 generation/performance runs for FP8,
CANN 9.2.0-beta.2, custom SDK       MXFP8, and MXFP4; not model-quality
3.1.0+fb774c4.c8v16                 parity.
Ascend 910 / 910B / 910_93          These A5 quantized attention paths are not
                                    supported; use native FA.

On the target NPU host, activate the CANN environment and check the public
API:

>sh
    python3 -c 'from mindiesd import quant_attention; assert callable(quant_attention)'
<
This import check does not verify native execution. Missing SDKs,
incompatible libraries, and operator failures raise errors rather than
falling back to native FA.

                *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-configure-attention*
Configure attention

Parameter        Type  Description                 Default
---------------  ----  --------------------------  ---------------------------
precision        str   bf16 selects native         Unset (existing native
                       floating-point FA; fp8,     selection)
                       mxfp8, or mxfp4 selects
                       MindIE-SD.
fp8_fa_mode      str   FP8 only; HIGH_PRECISION    HIGH_PRECISION
                       or C8V16_TILING512 (head
                       dimension 128).
head_chunk_size  int   MHA heads per SD call. Use  4
                       0 to disable chunking, or
                       another positive integer.
qk_rotation      bool  Apply online Q/K rotation   true, or false when the
                       before quantization. Not    checkpoint already includes
                       used by the native BF16     offline Q/K rotation
                       path.

`C8V16_TILING512` is an alternative FP8 compute/tiling mode for head
dimension 128. It changes the V block layout and the fused kernel's internal
precision setting; Q/K/V still pass through SDK quantization. Compare its
latency and numerical quality with `HIGH_PRECISION` on your workload before
choosing it. See the SDK implementation
https://gitcode.com/Ascend/MindIE-SD/blob/3.2.0/mindiesd/layers/flash_attn/fused_infer_attention_score.py.

For example, run MiniMax-H3 on two NPUs with FP8 C8V16 and the default chunk
size:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --model-path /models/MiniMax-H3 \
      --model-variant fl2va \
      --performance-mode manual \
      --num-gpus 2 --tp-size 2 \
      --vae-config.use-parallel-tiling false \
      --attention-backend fa \
      --attention-backend-config '{"precision":"fp8","fp8_fa_mode":"C8V16_TILING512"}' \
      --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \
      --save-output
<
For MXFP8 or MXFP4, use `'{"precision":"mxfp8"}'` or
`'{"precision":"mxfp4"}'`. Use `'{"precision":"bf16"}'` for a native
floating-point attention baseline, even when native MXFP8 is enabled in the
environment. The text encoder keeps its normal backend selection. Attention
precision is independent of linear-weight quantization. Add
`--quantization mxfp8` only if online MXFP8 linear weights are also wanted.

The SD path uses `attention_backend_config`; it does not need the native
`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ENABLE_MXFP8_ATTENTION` or
`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MXFP8_FA_HEAD_CHUNK_SIZE` variables. Head chunking applies
to dense and packed MHA, including a smaller final chunk. GQA is delegated
to the SDK without head chunking. Packed sequences remain isolated and H3
trailing padding is zeroed. Ordinary Ulysses is supported; causal attention,
nonzero dropout, Ring attention, and softmax LSE are unsupported.

Online rotation follows native Ascend FA's deterministic rotation and is
applied once by the SDK, before quantization. Checkpoints with offline Q/K
rotation default to no online rotation; explicitly enabling both is
rejected.

  Warning: ~

  MindIE-SD 3.2.0 pads MXFP4 sequence lengths to multiples of 512. The
  padded K/V positions participate in softmax. SGLang preserves this SDK
  behavior; validate numerical quality with the sequence lengths used by
  your workload.

          *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-validate-the-installation*
Validate the installation

Run from an installed SGLang checkout in the target Linux environment:

>sh
    # CPU adapter tests with a mocked SDK.
    pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_ascend_fa.py
<
These tests check adapter behavior without executing NPU kernels. They do
not establish model-quality parity; inspect generated outputs for your
workload.

   *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-using-sliding-tile-attention-sta*
Using Sliding Tile Attention (STA)

`STA_INFERENCE` also reads the per-layer STA parameters from the file named
by the `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_CONFIG` environment variable.

`STA_SEARCHING` writes one opaque sample name per submitted request; its
positive and negative loss files share that name in separate directories.
Repeating the same prompt adds a sample rather than overwriting the previous
one. Existing calibration JSON remains readable. Use a private calibration
directory; older files are not renamed or removed.

>sh
    # Pass the mask strategy file path via config
    SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_CONFIG=/abs/path/to/sta_config.json \
    sglang generate \
      --model-path <MODEL_PATH_OR_ID> \
      --prompt "..." \
      --attention-backend sliding_tile_attn \
      --attention-backend-config "mask_strategy_file_path=/abs/path/to/mask_strategy.json,STA_mode=STA_INFERENCE"
<

      *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-using-ascend-sparse-attention*
Using Ascend Sparse Attention

Use a Linux Ascend environment with the prerequisites above. Set
`MODEL_PATH` to a supported pipeline's local directory or Hugging Face
repository ID. This example uses one NPU with Ulysses degree 1, BF16 sparse
attention, and the shared BF16 FA executor for the first 10 and final 2
steps:

>sh
    MODEL_PATH="/path/to/pipeline"
    sglang generate \
      --model-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \
      --num-gpus 1 \
      --ulysses-degree 1 \
      --attention-backend ascend_sparse_attn \
      --attention-backend-config '{"sparse_type":"rf_v3","precision":"bf16","sparsity":0.6,"skip_first_steps":10,"skip_last_steps":2,"dense_kwargs":{"precision":"bf16"}}' \
      --prompt "A sailboat crossing a calm lake at sunrise"
<
For supported A5 operators, use `"precision":"mix"` for EagleQBSA sparse
steps. To select FP8 dense attention independently, set
`"dense_kwargs":{"precision":"fp8","fp8_fa_mode":"HIGH_PRECISION"}`. For
MXFP4 dense attention, use `"dense_kwargs":{"precision":"mxfp4"}` and any
supported MXFP4-specific options; omit FP8-specific options.

               *docs-sglang-diffusion-attention_backends-notes-for-rocm-/-mps*
Notes for ROCm / MPS

- ROCm: Instinct (CDNA, gfx9) GPUs default to `aiter`; use
  `--attention-backend torch_sdpa` on Radeon (RDNA) GPUs or when AITER is
  unavailable (`fa` also resolves to `torch_sdpa` on ROCm). On gfx1151 /
  Strix Halo (wave32), do not use `aiter` --- prefer `torch_sdpa` (image
  sets `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`).
- MPS: the platform implementation always uses `torch_sdpa`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cache-DiT Acceleration                *sglang-docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit*

Configure Cache-DiT acceleration for diffusion inference.

SGLang integrates Cache-DiT https://github.com/vipshop/cache-dit, a caching
acceleration engine for Diffusion Transformers (DiT), to achieve up to 1.69x
inference speedup with minimal quality loss.

OVERVIEW                            *docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-overview*

Cache-DiT uses intelligent caching strategies to skip redundant computation
in the denoising loop:

- DBCache (Dual Block Cache): Dynamically decides when to cache transformer
  blocks based on residual differences
- TaylorSeer: Uses Taylor expansion for calibration to optimize caching
  decisions
- DMD Calibrator: An exponential-basis forecasting calibrator (Dynamic Mode
  Decomposition, not Distribution Matching Distillation) that serves as a
  drop-in alternative to TaylorSeer's polynomial basis; strongest on
  flow-matching models
- SCM (Step Computation Masking): Step-level caching control for additional
  speedup

Cache-DiT also ships SVDQuant W4A4 (int4 / NVFP4) dynamic quantization,
which can be combined with DBCache caching (see
|docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-quantization|).

BASIC USAGE                      *docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-basic-usage*

Cache-DiT is a per-request switch: each request decides whether to run
cached or lossless, and requests with different Cache-DiT settings never
share a batch. The `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_*` environment variables remain
available as server-wide defaults for requests that leave the switch unset.

Enable it for a single generation:

>sh
    sglang generate --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
        --prompt "A beautiful sunset over the mountains" \
        --enable-cache-dit true
<
Or per request against a running server, via the OpenAI-compatible API:

>python
    client.images.generate(
        model="Qwen/Qwen-Image",
        prompt="A beautiful sunset over the mountains",
        extra_body={
            "enable_cache_dit": True,
            # optional knob overrides for this request only
            "cache_dit_params": {"residual_diff_threshold": 0.12, "scm_preset": "fast"},
        },
    )
<
`enable_cache_dit` accepts three states: `true` (on for this request),
`false` (off for this request, overriding the server default), and unset
(follow the `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED` server default). `cache_dit_params`
accepts the DBCache knobs (`Fn_compute_blocks`, `Bn_compute_blocks`,
`max_warmup_steps`, `residual_diff_threshold`,
`max_continuous_cached_steps`, `enable_taylorseer`, `taylorseer_order`), the
DMD knobs (`enable_dmd`, `dmd_history`, `dmd_rank`, `dmd_ridge`,
`dmd_svd_precision`; DMD and TaylorSeer are mutually exclusive calibrators
and cannot be enabled together), the SCM knobs (`scm_preset`,
`scm_compute_bins`, `scm_cache_bins`, `scm_policy`), and a nested
`secondary` dict with the DBCache knobs for the second transformer of
dual-DiT models (unset secondary keys inherit the request's primary values,
then the `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_SECONDARY_*` defaults).

To make Cache-DiT the default for every request instead, export the
environment variable when launching:

>sh
    SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED=true \
    sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image
<

DIFFUSERS BACKEND          *docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-diffusers-backend*

Cache-DiT supports loading acceleration configs from a custom YAML file. For
diffusers pipelines (`diffusers` backend), pass the YAML/JSON path via
`--cache-dit-config`. This flow requires cache-dit >= 1.2.0
(`cache_dit.load_configs`).

Single GPU inference    *docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-single-gpu-inference*

Define a `cache.yaml` file that contains:

- DBCache + TaylorSeer

>yaml
    cache_config:
      max_warmup_steps: 8
      warmup_interval: 2
      max_cached_steps: -1
      max_continuous_cached_steps: 2
      Fn_compute_blocks: 1
      Bn_compute_blocks: 0
      residual_diff_threshold: 0.12
      enable_taylorseer: true
      taylorseer_order: 1
<
Then apply the config with:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --backend diffusers \
      --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
      --cache-dit-config cache.yaml \
      --prompt "A beautiful sunset over the mountains"
<
- DBCache + TaylorSeer + SCM (Step Computation Mask)

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    cache_config:
      max_warmup_steps: 8
      warmup_interval: 2
      max_cached_steps: -1
      max_continuous_cached_steps: 2
      Fn_compute_blocks: 1
      Bn_compute_blocks: 0
      residual_diff_threshold: 0.12
      enable_taylorseer: true
      taylorseer_order: 1
      # Must set the num_inference_steps for SCM. The SCM will automatically
      # generate the steps computation mask based on the num_inference_steps.
      # Reference: https://cache-dit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/CACHE_API/#scm-steps-computation-masking
      num_inference_steps: 28
      steps_computation_mask: fast
<
- DBCache + TaylorSeer + SCM (Step Computation Mask) + Cache CFG

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    cache_config:
      max_warmup_steps: 8
      warmup_interval: 2
      max_cached_steps: -1
      max_continuous_cached_steps: 2
      Fn_compute_blocks: 1
      Bn_compute_blocks: 0
      residual_diff_threshold: 0.12
      enable_taylorseer: true
      taylorseer_order: 1
      num_inference_steps: 28
      steps_computation_mask: fast
      enable_sperate_cfg: true # e.g, Qwen-Image, Wan, Chroma, Ovis-Image, etc.
<
- DBCache + DMD Calibrator

Instead of TaylorSeer, you can use the DMD calibrator: an exponential-basis
forecasting calibrator that serves as a drop-in alternative to TaylorSeer's
polynomial basis. DMD models the cached feature stream as a linear dynamical
system (`Y_{t+1} ~= A @ Y_t`), forecasts cached features from the fitted
eigen-modes, and stays accurate over longer cache skips where polynomial
extrapolation diverges. DMD here refers to Dynamic Mode Decomposition
(Schmid 2010), not Distribution Matching Distillation. DMD works best on
flow-matching models (e.g., FLUX), while TaylorSeer is often better on
DDPM-style models --- try both. DMD and TaylorSeer are mutually exclusive
--- enable only one of `enable_dmd` / `enable_taylorseer`:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    cache_config:
      max_warmup_steps: 8
      warmup_interval: 2
      max_cached_steps: -1
      max_continuous_cached_steps: 2
      Fn_compute_blocks: 1
      Bn_compute_blocks: 0 # Bn=0 since the DMD calibrator replaces the Bn calibrator
      residual_diff_threshold: 0.12
      enable_dmd: true
      dmd_history: 6 # snapshot window length, 5-6 typical
      dmd_svd_precision: "medium" # "low", "medium" or "high"
<
A `dmd_history` window of 5--6 snapshots is typically the sweet spot ---
longer histories do not always help, because the feature dynamics drift
across timesteps. With fewer than 4 uniformly spaced snapshots available,
DMD transparently falls back to the Taylor expansion it maintains
internally. See the Cache-DiT DMD documentation
https://cache-dit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/CACHE_API/#dmd-calibrator-dynamic-mode-decomposition
for the mathematical principle and quantitative comparisons. A ready-made
config is available at examples/configs/cache_dmd.yaml
https://github.com/vipshop/cache-dit/blob/main/examples/configs/cache_dmd.yaml
in the Cache-DiT repository. Apply it with the same `--cache-dit-config`
flag:

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --backend diffusers \
      --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
      --cache-dit-config cache_dmd.yaml \
      --prompt "A beautiful sunset over the mountains"
<

Distributed inference  *docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-distributed-inference*

- 1D Parallelism

Define a parallelism only config yaml `parallel.yaml` file that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: auto
      attention_backend: native
<
Then, apply the distributed inference acceleration config from yaml.
`ulysses_size: auto` means that cache-dit will auto detect the `world_size`
as the ulysses_size. Otherwise, you should manually set it as specific int
number, e.g, 4.

Then apply the distributed config with: (Note: please add `--num-gpus N` to
specify the number of gpus for distributed inference)

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --backend diffusers \
      --num-gpus 4 \
      --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
      --cache-dit-config parallel.yaml \
      --prompt "A futuristic cityscape at sunset"
<
- 2D Parallelism

You can also define a 2D parallelism config yaml `parallel_2d.yaml` file
that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: auto
      tp_size: 2
      attention_backend: native
<
Then, apply the 2D parallelism config from yaml. Here `tp_size: 2` means
using tensor parallelism with size 2. The `ulysses_size: auto` means that
cache-dit will auto detect the `world_size // tp_size` as the ulysses_size.

- 3D Parallelism

You can also define a 3D parallelism config yaml `parallel_3d.yaml` file
that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: 2
      ring_size: 2
      tp_size: 2
      attention_backend: native
<
Then, apply the 3D parallelism config from yaml. Here `ulysses_size: 2`,
`ring_size: 2`, `tp_size: 2` means using ulysses parallelism with size 2,
ring parallelism with size 2 and tensor parallelism with size 2.

- Ulysses Anything Attention

To enable Ulysses Anything Attention, you can define a parallelism config
yaml `parallel_uaa.yaml` file that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: auto
      attention_backend: native
      ulysses_anything: true
<
- Ulysses FP8 Communication

For device that don't have NVLink support, you can enable Ulysses FP8
Communication to further reduce the communication overhead. You can define a
parallelism config yaml `parallel_fp8.yaml` file that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: auto
      attention_backend: native
      ulysses_float8: true
<
- Async Ulysses CP

You can also enable async ulysses CP to overlap the communication and
computation. Define a parallelism config yaml `parallel_async.yaml` file
that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: auto
      attention_backend: native
      ulysses_async: true # Now, only support for FLUX.1, Qwen-Image, Ovis-Image and Z-Image.
<
Then, apply the config from yaml. Here `ulysses_async: true` means enabling
async ulysses CP.

- TE-P and VAE-P

You can also specify the extra parallel modules in the yaml config. For
example, define a parallelism config yaml `parallel_extra.yaml` file that
contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    parallelism_config:
      ulysses_size: auto
      attention_backend: native
      extra_parallel_modules: ["text_encoder", "vae"]
<

                *docs-sglang-diffusion-cache_dit-hybrid-cache-and-parallelism*
Hybrid Cache and Parallelism

Define a hybrid cache and parallel acceleration config yaml `hybrid.yaml`
file that contains:

[Config]

[Config]Config

>yaml
    cache_config:
      max_warmup_steps: 8
      warmup_interval: 2
      max_cached_steps: -1
      max_continuous_cached_steps: 2
      Fn_compute_blocks: 1
      Bn_compute_blocks: 0
      residual_diff_threshold: 0.12
      enable_taylorseer: true
      taylorseer_order: 1

      attention_backend: native
      extra_parallel_modules: ["text_encoder", "vae"]
<
Then, apply the hybrid cache and parallel acceleration config from yaml.

>sh
    sglang generate \
      --backend diffusers \
      --num-gpus 4 \
      --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image \
